title: Reimagining consumer behaviour in retailing: An AI-adapted stimulus-organism-response model
abstract: Based on the classical Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) paradigm, this conceptual paper builds a theoretical model which proposes that AI-driven stimuli positively affect consumer satisfaction, purchase intention and repurchase intention. The paper takes a conceptual and theory building approach, bringing together literature on AI, retailing, and consumer behavior, and classical environmental-psychology theorising on the SOR paradigm to create a dual-pathway AI adapted SOR model in three iterative stages. There were two types of organismic paths in the model: a satisfaction-based path (security, ease of use, delivery, e-service, experience) and a purchase-intention-based path (AI-ease of use, pre-purchase satisfaction, online trust, previous experience) both leading to the repurchase intention, which were moderated by the technology readiness, privacy concern, algorithmic trust, and retail channel. The construction of a set of ten formal propositions which guide empirical testing. The model is conceptual and propositions are yet to be tested through the empirical studies. Structural equation modelling of the dual pathways, multi-group testing of the moderating propositions, and experimental testing of the moderating propositions, in addition to longitudinal designs testing the learning-based propositions of the model, all features among the priority areas. This paper is one of the first theoretical extensions of the SOR paradigm specific to adaptive, non-transparent, and channel-spanning nature of the AI-based retail stimuli, and transfers a distinct empirical literature into a single, falsifiable model.

title: Federated Learning and Generative AI for Privacy-Preserving Knowledge Transfer in Design Education
abstract: Cross-organizational design collaboration faces a fundamental paradox where enterprises possess valuable practical knowledge essential for student development, yet data privacy regulations prevent direct sharing. This study develops a federated learning-integrated generative AI platform addressing privacy-preserving knowledge transfer between industry and educational institutions while systematically enhancing student innovation capabilities. The platform employs a three-layer cloud-edge-end architecture incorporating dynamic quality-weighted federated aggregation with proximal regularization for non-IID heterogeneity, differential privacy mechanisms for formal privacy guarantees, and LoRA-adapted generative models for domain-specific design synthesis. Cross-domain knowledge fusion utilizes adversarial domain adaptation and knowledge distillation to harmonize heterogeneous expertise. Experiments on ShapeNet 3D dataset (51,300 models, 55 categories) demonstrate 72.3% classification accuracy with 23% communication overhead reduction compared to standard federated baselines. Generated designs achieve FID=22.7 and IS=3.79, validated through expert evaluation. Controlled educational trials with 42 students show significant capability improvements: design quality (+16.3 points), AI literacy (+25.6 points), and collaboration ability (+14.9 points), all statistically significant (p<0.01). This work pioneers the integration of federated learning with generative AI for design education, establishing a privacy-utility equilibrium that enables authentic industry knowledge exposure without raw data exchange, thereby advancing both collaborative innovation infrastructure and AI-literate design talent cultivation.

title: Few-shot classification of underwater multi-label images through image-conditioned prompt learning and language-image interaction
abstract: Abstract To address the inherent degradation of underwater images induced by water’s optical properties and the prohibitive cost of data acquisition and annotation, which are key constraints limiting the applicability of traditional methods in few-shot learning scenarios, this study proposes a dedicated model for few-shot underwater optical multi-label image classification (UOMIC). The proposed framework integrates three synergistic components to enhance classification performance: Image-Conditioned Learnable Prompts modulate textual features to effectively alleviate the semantic mismatch between images and text in complex underwater environments. language-image interaction module, grounded in attention mechanisms, precisely captures fine-grained details across heterogeneous image regions while simultaneously modeling global semantics and long-range dependencies. The FFN-Based Gated Adapter strengthens multi-scale feature representation capabilities, thereby improving the model’s robustness in classifying complex underwater objects under few-shot constraints. Comprehensive experiments conducted on multiple underwater datasets demonstrate that the proposed UOMIC model exhibits superior specificity and robustness on underwater object datasets, providing a novel technical paradigm for addressing challenging underwater computer vision tasks.

title: Exact Risk-Complexity Laws for Projective Boundaries in Scenario Optimization and Distribution-Free Certification
abstract: Scenario optimization, conformal prediction, and related distribution-free certification methods use finite samples to construct decisions or prediction sets with violation-risk guarantees for fresh observations. In several classical settings, the conditional violation risk follows an exact beta law, whose tail has a beta-binomial representation and whose parameter is a support, calibration, or compression dimension. This paper identifies the deterministic boundary mechanism behind these formulas and derives the corresponding law when the observed boundary size is random. A decision rule is represented by an acceptance set for future observations, together with a boundary map selecting the sample points responsible for that set. The resulting pair is called a {\em proper projective boundary scheme} when held-out samples are accepted precisely if the full-sample boundary is retained, and accepted non-boundary samples can be deleted without changing that boundary. For every such scheme, the conditional law of the violation risk given the observed boundary size is determined by the boundary's cross-sample complexity profile. A stable profile yields the usual beta law, whereas a varying profile produces an exact profile correction. The framework covers scalar order-statistic calibration, support-reconstructive scenario programs, cascaded support-removal certificates, coordinatewise envelopes, and Pareto-frontier calibration with vector scores. It also yields conditional probabilistic certificates and a no-go result explaining why observed complexity alone is insufficient.

The resulting pair is called a {\em proper projective boundary scheme} when held-out samples are accepted precisely if the full-sample boundary is retained, and accepted non-boundary samples can be deleted without changing that boundary. For every such scheme, the conditional law of the violation risk given the observed boundary size is determined by the boundary's cross-sample complexity profile. A stable profile yields the usual beta law, whereas a varying profile produces an exact profile correction. The framework covers scalar order-statistic calibration, support-reconstructive scenario programs, cascaded support-removal certificates, coordinatewise envelopes, and Pareto-frontier calibration with vector scores. It also yields conditional probabilistic certificates and a no-go result explaining why observed complexity alone is insufficient.

title: Tangent fermions can restore vacuum stability of discrete-time Dirac models
abstract: The Dirac quantum walk (a 1+1 dimensional space-time discretization of the Dirac equation) has a $2μ$ mass gap both at the center and at the corner of the quasi-energy-momentum Brillouin zone. Gupta and Short recently noted [Quantum 9, 1845 (2025)] that the Dirac vacuum can create a particle-hole pair at the zone corner with the release of an energy $2μ$ to the environment. They removed this vacuum instability at the expense of fermion doubling, the appearance of a second low-energy Dirac cone. Here we show that an alternative discretization scheme, with a tangent rather than a sine dispersion relation, offers stability while retaining a single Dirac cone. The key step is the Cayley transformation from the unit circle of Floquet eigenvalues $e^{-i\varepsilon}$ to the real line of unbounded energies $E=2\tan(\varepsilon/2)$. We compute the Schwinger effect (particle-hole pair creation in a uniform electric field) for tangent fermions and show that the pair-production rate agrees with the continuum result for a single Dirac cone. The zone corner is exactly decoupled if the scalar potential is coupled through the Hermitian generator of the quantum map. If it is coupled as a split operator, in order to preserve exact gauge invariance on the lattice, the corner does contribute - with a weight that vanishes quadratically with the lattice constants, in contrast to the Dirac quantum walk where the zone-corner instability survives the continuum limit.

title: Detecting entanglement from few partial transpose moments and their decay via weight enumerators
abstract: Abstract In light of the rapid experimental development of quantum devices, tools for estimating quantum properties, particularly entanglement, must be improved to keep pace. The p 3 -PPT criterion is an experimentally viable relaxation of the well-known positive partial transposition (PPT) criterion for the certification of quantum entanglement. Recently, it has been generalized to various families of entanglement criteria based on the PT moments p k = Tr [ ( ρ Γ ) k ] , where ρ Γ denotes the partially transposed density matrix of a quantum state ρ . title: Estrategias de discurso y persuasión mediante IA para la divulgación de innovaciones industriales sostenibles: guía de indicaciones, repositorio de prompts optimizados (COSTAR) y hoja de ruta de adopción
abstract: Material complementario del Trabajo Fin de Grado en Ingeniería Química (Universidad Politécnica de Madrid, 2026) sobre el uso de inteligencia artificial generativa con instrucciones estructuradas conforme al marco COSTAR para la divulgación de sostenibilidad industrial. El paquete reúne tres entregables construidos sobre la arquitectura COSTAR validada y el banco de sesenta tareas. La guía de indicaciones es un manual de uso del sistema, organizado en nueve apartados, pensado para perfiles técnicos sin formación en ingeniería de prompts. El repositorio de prompts optimizados conserva los prompts finales validados, comentarios de calidad, la evolución entre la versión inicial y la final, respuestas de ejemplo para un subconjunto de diez tareas y la bitácora completa del experimento con 796 registros. La hoja de ruta preliminar de adopción describe seis fases de incorporación, fija la supervisión humana como condición estructural y recoge riesgos, medidas de mitigación y criterios de eficiencia basados en tokens. Los materiales tienen carácter preliminar y exploratorio; su aplicación en contextos reales requiere adaptación y validación posterior.

title: Quantum HS Communication: Synchronization Structures Through Entanglement
abstract: This work proposes a concept of using quantum entanglement for synchronizing semantic structures between remote observers without the need for classical data transmission. In contrast to traditional interpretations of the no-communication theorem, we demonstrate that quantum correlation can be used for instantaneous synchronization of complex patterns, the information extraction of which occurs through holistic pattern analysis. The proposed QHSC (Quantum HS Communication) protocol introduces a novel multi-level verification framework that distinguishes Alice's correlated signal from Bob's local noise through structural pattern matching. We show that the probability of random generation of a complete semantic pattern by local noise tends to zero, while quantum correlation ensures deterministic pattern matching between Alice and Bob.Furthermore, we demonstrate that the algorithmic core of QHSC possesses the property of physical layer agnosticism and can be deployed on existing classical communication channels, solving critical problems of resilient communication in challenging environments.

title: CatInspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, CatInspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (CIMA), inspired by the hunting behavior of cats. CIMA leverages the cat's agility, hunting strategy, and environmental awareness to effectively navigate complex optimization landscapes. The algorithm incorporates key feline characteristics into its core mechanisms, including a 'stalking' phase for exploration, a 'pounce' phase for exploitation, and a 'scanning' phase for global assessment. Mathematical formulations are presented to detail the algorithm's parameters and operations. The performance of CIMA is evaluated on a variety of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitiveness and potential for solving challenging real-world optimization tasks. The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency are highlighted, making it a viable alternative to existing metaheuristic techniques. Specifically, we explore the impact of parameter tuning on the algorithm's convergence rate and solution quality. The results show that CIMA exhibits robust performance across different problem types, suggesting its general applicability and potential for further development.

title: Recursive Self-Similarity in Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores the potential of recursive self-similarity within evolutionary algorithms to achieve significantly improved performance on complex optimization problems. We propose a novel algorithm, dubbed "Recursive Self-Similarity," that leverages iterative refinement to generate solutions exhibiting a degree of self-similarity at different scales. This approach aims to accelerate convergence and enable the discovery of optimal solutions to challenging problems by mimicking the inherent structure of complex systems. The core mechanism centers around a recursive refinement step, which systematically modifies a solution while maintaining a pattern of self-reflection. We present a detailed analysis of the algorithm's effectiveness, demonstrating its superior performance compared to traditional evolutionary algorithms in several benchmark scenarios. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential applications and limitations of this new methodology.

title: Title: Quantum Information Super-Resolution Computation
abstract: Quantum information processing has emerged as a transformative technology with significant potential across diverse fields, including image processing and data analysis. This paper presents a novel approach to super-resolution computation leveraging the unique properties of quantum information – specifically, superposition and entanglement – to achieve significantly improved results compared to classical methods. We propose a new algorithm that utilizes a quantum-enhanced measurement process to precisely determine pixel values, ultimately leading to enhanced image reconstruction and data interpretation. The core claim of this work is the design of a quantum-informed super-resolution algorithm that surpasses current state-of-the-art performance, particularly in scenarios demanding high-fidelity image reconstruction. This research explores the potential of quantum entanglement and superposition to address challenges inherent in traditional super-resolution techniques. We will detail the underlying mathematical framework, provide a simplified implementation, and discuss the theoretical implications of this approach.

title: 基于几何场论的自适应机器学习算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning algorithm based on geometric field theory, aiming to enhance model generalization and adaptability. Traditional machine learning often relies on handcrafted features, limiting the model's ability to effectively learn from data. We propose a method that leverages the inherent geometric structure of data to learn a more robust and flexible model. This approach utilizes a core mechanism centered around the transformation of data into a geometric field, enabling the algorithm to implicitly capture complex relationships and dependencies. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through several experiments, showcasing improved performance compared to conventional methods across various datasets. The core claim is that this geometric field theory-based algorithm significantly improves the model's robustness and adaptability.

title: ## Brush Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of Brush Mice
abstract: This paper presents Brush Mouse, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of brush mice. These rodents employ a unique "brushing" strategy, systematically exploring their environment to locate food sources. This algorithm leverages this strategy through a dynamic exploration-exploitation process, utilizing a virtual "brush" to iteratively refine a solution set. Brush Mouse incorporates key elements of the brushing behavior, including a probabilistic movement pattern, adaptive step size control, and a memory mechanism for retaining promising regions. The algorithm is designed for a wide range of optimization problems, particularly those with complex, non-convex landscapes. The performance of Brush Mouse is evaluated across a series of benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions. The core innovation lies in the algorithm's ability to balance exploration and exploitation effectively, leading to improved convergence rates and solution quality compared to traditional metaheuristic approaches. The algorithm's parameters are designed to be easily tunable, offering flexibility in adapting it to specific problem characteristics. Experimental results demonstrate Brush Mouse's competitive performance, highlighting its potential as a valuable addition to the metaheuristic optimization toolbox.

title: Brazilian Slender Opossum Optimization Algorithm (BSOA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Brazilian Slender Opossum Optimization Algorithm (BSOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Brazilian slender opossum (*Didilophos arcanus*). The algorithm mimics the opossum's unique ability to locate food sources in complex terrains using a combination of movement strategies, including climbing, leaping, and searching. BSOA leverages a population-based search approach with adaptive mutation and a novel fitness evaluation method that incorporates terrain complexity. The algorithm employs a dynamic population size, adaptive mutation rates, and a simulated terrain landscape to effectively explore and exploit the search space. The core components of BSOA include a terrain representation, a movement strategy based on opossum behavior, and an adaptive fitness function. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency in solving challenging optimization tasks. The results show that BSOA exhibits competitive performance compared to existing metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems with complex landscapes and high dimensionality. The key contributions of this work are the innovative terrain representation, the behavioral-inspired movement strategy, and the adaptive fitness function, which collectively contribute to the algorithm's robust optimization capabilities.

title: ## Boomer: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of Boomer Birds
abstract: This paper presents Boomer, a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed for optimization problems. The algorithm's inspiration stems from the unique foraging behavior of Boomer birds, specifically their tendency to rapidly switch between different search areas and exhibit a "boom-and-bust" strategy in their food collection. Boomer leverages these characteristics through a dynamic exploration and exploitation phase, combined with a novel population diversity maintenance mechanism. The algorithm operates by maintaining a population of potential solutions and iteratively refining them. A key component is the 'Boom' phase, which involves a rapid, random perturbation of the population, and the 'Bust' phase, which concentrates on exploiting promising regions. The performance of Boomer is evaluated on a selection of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The algorithm's parameters are tuned to balance exploration and exploitation, leading to robust performance across various problem landscapes. Future research directions include incorporating adaptive parameter control and exploring its applicability to complex, real-world problems.

title: Information Theory-Based Adaptive Encryption Protocol
abstract: This paper proposes a novel information-theoretic adaptive encryption protocol designed to enhance both security and performance. Traditional cryptographic methods rely on static parameters, limiting flexibility and potentially compromising security in dynamic environments. This work introduces a dynamic adjustment mechanism based on information theory, allowing the protocol to dynamically adjust encryption strength and algorithm parameters based on the input data's characteristics. The core mechanism leverages the concepts of entropy, robustness, and statistical properties to achieve adaptive encryption. This design offers a significant improvement in security and efficiency compared to static cryptographic approaches, particularly in scenarios involving evolving data or unpredictable attacks.

title: A Guide to the Logic Series Papers
abstract: A Guide to the Logic Series Papers This guide organizes the logic series papers into four parts by time and theme: the discovery process (before 9/1) → after the three dimensions were determined → the theoretical cornerstones → applications. I. Pre-9/1 Versions — The Discovery Process, as Recorded Positioning: These record the discovery process of the logical theory; they can be consulted for reference and contain many errors. title: Blanford's Fruit Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Fruit Bat Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed Blanford's Fruit Bat Algorithm (BFBA), inspired by the foraging behavior of Blanford's fruit bats. These bats utilize a unique "return-to-base" strategy combined with a random search pattern. BFBA leverages this behavior to navigate a search space, aiming to find optimal solutions to complex optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates parameters mimicking bat flight characteristics, including flight radius, flight speed, and echo detection. Specifically, the algorithm's core mechanism involves a probabilistic transition between a 'return-to-base' phase and a 'random search' phase, governed by the bat's echo reception probability. The performance of BFBA is evaluated through a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive advantage compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The key mathematical formulations within the BFBA are presented, detailing the movement equations and the probability distributions influencing the search process. The results indicate that BFBA offers a robust and efficient approach to tackling diverse optimization challenges.

title: Title: Stability Analysis and Improvement of Non-Linear Models
abstract: This paper explores the stability of non-linear models, particularly in the context of large and high-dimensional datasets. We introduce a novel stability analysis framework that dynamically adjusts stability metrics based on model parameter changes, offering a more robust and adaptable approach. The core mechanism involves the integration of a "dynamic stability indicator," which automatically adjusts the indicator based on parameter variations, and optimization of the overall model stability. This work aims to address the limitations of traditional stability analysis methods by focusing on dynamic behavior and providing a framework for enhanced model robustness.

title: Ultracomputing: A Vision for Quantum-Native Artificial Ultraintelligence (AUI)
abstract: A vision paper introducing Ultracomputing, a proposed quantum-native computing paradigm integrating fault-tolerant quantum computing, classical supercomputing, quantum networking, and quantum-native software; Artificial Ultraintelligence (AUI) as the final stage of artificial superintelligence enabled by such architectures; and Q-I/O (QIO), a conceptual roadmap from today's hybrid AI systems toward fully quantum-native intelligence.

title: Natural Language Processing Methods for the Analysis of Project Applications within the IPMA Methodology
abstract: Purpose: This study explores how natural language processing (NLP) can support the analysis and classification of project applications framed within the IPMA Individual Competence Baseline (ICB 4.0), addressing the labour-intensive nature of manually reviewing large volumes of funding applications.Design/Methodology/Approach: Using a corpus of 6,031 Polish-language projectapplication titles, we apply the Polish transformer language model HerBERT to represent the titles as embeddings and to classify them into the three IPMA competence areas (Perspective, People and Practice) by means of cosine similarity, validated against expert judgement on a sample ( ).This matching procedure is complemented by unsupervised Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modelling, with the number of topics selected using coherence and perplexity.Findings: HerBERT-based classification reached about agreement with expert assessment; performance varied markedly across the competence areas and between the maximum-and median-similarity aggregation rules.LDA revealed interpretable themes: the two-topic grouping separated a growth-and-recovery orientation from a stabilitymaintenance orientation, whereas the eight-topic solution disaggregated these into finer strategic and operational themes (e.g., resilience, digitalisation, crisis management and financial stability).

title: A Quantum-Memetic Hybrid Framework for Combinatorial Optimization: Synergistic Integration of Superposition-Based Exploration with Adaptive Exploitation
abstract: The effective resolution of non-deterministic polynomial time hard (NP-hard) combinatorial optimization problems requires a delicate balance between global exploration and local exploitation. While Quantum-Inspired Algorithms (QIAs) leverage principles of superposition to explore vast search spaces, they often lack the fine-grained exploitation capabilities of classical heuristics. To address this limitation, we propose the Quantum-Memetic Hybrid Algorithm (QMHA), a component-based framework that synergistically integrates qubit-based global search with adaptive classical refinement. The QMHA architecture explicitly coordinates five distinct algorithmic components: (1) quantum rotation gates for exploration, (2) a problem-aware memetic operator for immediate solution refinement, (3) an adaptive learning rate schedule, (4) periodic local search, and (5) a stagnation-based population reset for diversity management. We rigorously evaluate the framework against nine established metaheuristics, including Genetic Algorithms (GA), Differential Evolution (DE), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Simulated Annealing (SA), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), MAX-MIN Ant System (MMAS), Memetic Algorithms (MA), Quantum Evolutionary Algorithm (QEA), and Harmony Search (HS), across a comprehensive benchmark suite comprising six NP-hard problem families: constrained combinatorial (Knapsack), graph-based (Max-Cut), permutation-based (TSP), constraint satisfaction (Graph Coloring), bin optimization (Bin Packing), and scheduling (Flow Shop Scheduling), as well as real-world machine learning (Feature Selection) problems and the continuous Congress on Evolutionary Computation (CEC) 2022 benchmark. Statistical analysis using Friedman tests and Nemenyi post hoc comparisons confirms that QMHA achieves a statistically significant performance advantage (p<0.004) and superior average rank (1.5) compared to component baselines and state-of-the-art competitors. Comprehensive analyses include computational complexity profiling, parameter sensitivity mapping, scalability testing up to D=2000, noise robustness evaluation, variable correlation degradation analysis, a six-component ablation study, exploration–exploitation dynamics tracking, integration mechanism comparison across five architectures, and a multi-objective extension feasibility study. The proposed framework offers a robust, verified approach to hybrid optimization without relying on biological metaphors.

title: Analisis Sentimen Real-Time Ulasan Pengguna Aplikasi PineDrama pada Google Play Store Menggunakan Metode Support Vector Machine (SVM)
abstract: The increasing number of user reviews on the Google Play Store provides valuable information for app developers in evaluating service quality. However, the increasing number of reviews makes manual analysis less effective. This study aims to develop a near real-time sentiment analysis system for PineDrama app reviews using the Support Vector Machine (SVM) method with Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) weighting. The system is designed to automatically retrieve the latest reviews using Google Play Scraper, then perform a preprocessing process that includes case folding, cleaning, normalization, stopword removal, and stemming. Next, the data is classified into positive, neutral, and negative sentiments using a trained SVM model. The classification results are stored in a SQLite database and displayed through a Flask-based dashboard that is updated periodically using a scheduler. Based on the test results, the SVM model produces an accuracy of 91.06%, with a precision value of 92.50%, a recall of 91.06%, and an F1-score of 91.50%, indicating that the model has good performance in classifying review sentiments. The developed system also successfully displays analysis results in near real-time, thus helping the process of monitoring user opinions on the PineDrama application more quickly and efficiently.

title: TRUSTX-LUNG: EXPLAINABLE DEEP ENSEMBLE INTELLIGENCE FOR LUNG CANCER DETECTION
abstract: This study is a proposal of an integrative framework using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) and Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) to provide trustworthy and explainable explanations in the context of a deep ensemble model designed to classify pulmonary carcinoma. Three different pre-trained models, ResNet50, DenseNet121, and EfficientNetB0, and a deep ensemble model were used in this research approach. The paper outlines the methodological pathway that starts with the preprocessing of the high-resolution computed tomography (CT) images, followed by image enhancement and feature extraction through convolution neural network architectures. As there is no clear suggestion of which pre-trained model gives the best performance as compared to others, an ensemble approach has been introduced. The ensemble approach is a combination of multiple deep learning models that combine predictions to provide better accuracy and less variance between the different model predictions. Two leading post-hoc explainability techniques, Grad-CAM and LIME, are used to make the model interpretable when applied to clinical situations. The experimental assessment performed on image datasets of lung cancer from the computed tomography (CT) modality demonstrates that ensemble learning with these XAI techniques increases the diagnostic outcomes and the transparency. The deep ensemble model achieved 0.972 of accuracy, while ResNet50, DenseNet121, and EfficientNetB0 achieved 0.94, 0.9358, and 0.94 of accuracy, respectively. The results clearly indicate the regions of interest and the diagnostic features that help in the detection of lung cancer and boost the clinical confidence in the system. Possible problems, including image quality differences and the computational load of ensemble methods, are also addressed, and methods of optimization and implementation are suggested. In conclusion, the results illustrate that the use of Grad-CAM and LIME in a deep ensemble framework is beneficial for achieving excellent prediction accuracy and delivering interpretable insights that are essential for clinical decision-making and follow-up treatment of patients.

title: Histochemical stains in diagnostic histopathology: Principles, applications, and artificial intelligence perspectives
abstract: Histochemical staining remains fundamental to diagnostic histopathology, providing structural and functional information that complements routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) evaluation. Despite advances in immunohistochemistry, molecular diagnostics, and digital pathology, traditional histochemical stains continue to play essential roles in detecting microorganisms, extracellular matrix components, mucins, lipids, fibrin, elastic fibers, calcification, and pathological tissue deposits. However, their diagnostic applications and the emerging role of artificial intelligence (AI) in histochemical stain analysis remain underrepresented in contemporary literature. A targeted narrative review was conducted using PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar to identify peer-reviewed studies, technical reports, and guidelines published between 1990 and 2026. Literature addressing both conventional histochemical applications and emerging digital pathology and AI-based approaches was critically synthesized. This review summarizes the principles, diagnostic utility, technical considerations, and limitations of commonly used histochemical stains, including H&E, Gram, Giemsa, Ziehl–Neelsen, Grocott–Gomori methenamine silver, Periodic Acid–Schiff, Alcian Blue/PAS, Oil Red O, Gordon & Sweets, Masson’s trichrome, Verhoeff–Van Gieson, Martius Scarlet Blue, Congo red, Perls’ Prussian blue, and Von Kossa. It also provides a comprehensive overview of the current evidence supporting AI applications across individual histochemical stains, highlighting validated applications for H&E, reticulin, and Congo red, emerging evidence for several other stains, and important knowledge gaps requiring further investigation. By integrating conventional histochemistry with digital pathology and AI, this review identifies future research priorities and underscores the continuing importance of histochemical stains as indispensable components of precision pathology.

title: Robustness-Enhanced Quantum Integrated Sensing and Communication Networks Based on Bivariate Bicycle Codes Scheme
abstract: Quantum integrated sensing and communication (QISAC) enables simultaneous parameter estimation and secure information transmission based on shared entanglement resources, making it a promising research direction for future quantum information networks. In practical quantum channels, however, depolarizing noise, decoherence, and potential eavesdropping perturbations may degrade entanglement resources, increase the quantum bit error rate, and reduce both secrecy capacity and sensing performance. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a coding-enhanced QISAC (CE-QISAC) scheme. Based on the shared entanglement framework of existing QISAC protocols, the proposed scheme incorporates Bivariate Bicycle (BB) quantum low-density parity-check codes and a low-complexity belief propagation with localized statistics decoding (BP-LSD) algorithm to protect transmitted quantum states through error correction, thereby reducing the logical quantum bit error rate. The secrecy capacity under coding enhancement is analyzed according to the decoded logical error rate, while the waterfall effect of BB codes is further exploited to improve security detection sensitivity. Results show that the proposed scheme maintains high secrecy capacity in the nominal noise regime, mitigates the impact of depolarizing noise on parameter estimation, and reduces decoding complexity, providing a feasible approach for quantum integrated sensing and secure direct communication over noisy quantum channels.

title: Optimization of PMGRA-based gas geochemical survey for gold exploration in alpine meadow-covered areas: a case study of the Jiagantan gold deposit, West Qinling
abstract: Abstract Soil gas geochemical surveying is an effective tool for detecting concealed mineralization in covered areas. In this study, a Portable Multi-Component Gas Rapid Analyzer (PMGRA) was used to conduct controlled gas geochemical experiments at the Jiagantan gold deposit in the Gannan alpine meadow-covered area, West Qinling orogen. The responses of H 2 S, SO 2 , and CO 2 were evaluated under different temperature (0–10°C, 12–20°C, 22–28°C) and depth (8-12 cm, 55-65 cm, 90-110 cm) conditions. Results show that gas concentrations increase systematically with temperature. The most pronounced anomalies occur at 105 cm depth (B-C horizon), followed by 12 cm (A0 horizon), while the weakest anomalies are observed at 60 cm (A1 horizon). This pattern is consistent with the supergene geochemical characteristics of gold in alpine meadow areas. Based on these results, optimized survey parameters are proposed: sampling at the A0 horizon (∼12 cm) under warm conditions (>20°C), considering that the B-C horizon (∼105 cm) is often composed of frozen soil in alpine meadow areas, making it difficult and costly to sample. Preliminary anomaly thresholds for the Jiagantan deposit are H 2 S > 0.1 ppm, SO 2 > 0.03 ppm, and CO 2 > 2500 ppm. This study demonstrates that PMGRA-based gas geochemical surveying is an effective and rapid method for gold exploration in alpine meadow-covered terrains.

title: Reliable cross-view neighborhood relation transfer and high-order semantic structure mining for incomplete multi-view partial multi-label classification
abstract: Multi-view multi-label classification has attracted increasing attention because it can characterize complex real-world data from multiple perspectives. However, the simultaneous presence of missing views and labels often causes incomplete feature information and uncertain data distributions, hindering the extraction of discriminative semantics. To address this problem, we propose a unified framework termed Re liable C ross-View Neighborhood Relation Transfer and H igh-Order S emantic Structure M ining (ReCHSM). Specifically, we design a reliable cross-view completion mechanism that transfers neighborhood relations from observed views to reconstruct missing ones. To reduce erroneous transfer caused by cross-view heterogeneity, the mechanism evaluates candidate-neighbor reliability and employs a lightweight nonlinear network to refine the reconstructed features. To further extract structural information from the completed representations, we introduce a random-walk-based strategy that propagates the repaired local neighborhoods to capture high-order semantic dependencies. Furthermore, considering that individual views provide different discriminative information and that the quality of completed views may vary, we develop a label-semantic-consistency-driven module to assess view quality and adaptively assign fusion weights. Extensive experiments on five public datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitive performance of ReCHSM.

title: Public‐Key Quantum Signature Protocol Based on Generalized Isometric Tensor
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents a one‐time quantum public‐key signature protocol for classical messages that integrates message‐level generalized‐isometric‐tensor compression, a Full Quantum One‐Way Function (Full QOWF), public control‐dependent unitary encoding, and symmetric‐subspace quantum‐signature compression. The message‐level compressor reduces the message‐dependent length from to , while the transcript digest binds the message, compression metadata, compressed length, and one‐time public‐key identifier. For each control position, independent quantum private‐key branches are generated and mapped to public‐key states by the Full QOWF. The selected signature tag is encoded by a public unitary, and its identical copies are compressed in the symmetric subspace before transmission. Verification decompresses each block, reverses the unitary encoding, evaluates the Full QOWF, and performs repeated SWAP tests against authenticated public‐key copies. Under ideal implementation, honest signatures are accepted with probability one. Conditional one‐time unforgeability is established under quantum second‐preimage resistance, authenticated finite‐copy public‐key distribution, and bounded‐copy accepting‐preimage generation hardness. The online signature cost is reduced to qubits; for and , each repeated block decreases from 2048 to 507 transmitted qubits.

title: Randomized‐Grid Search for Time‐Efficient Hyperparameter Tuning in Cardiovascular Disease Classification
abstract: ABSTRACT Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are serious illnesses of the heart, which require accurate diagnosis to prevent fatal consequences. Hyperparameter tuning plays a critical role in optimizing machine learning (ML) model performance by selecting suitable parameter configurations for improved accuracy and generalization. Grid search systematically evaluates predefined hyperparameter combinations, whereas random search selects configurations randomly, enabling broader exploration at reduced computational cost. An efficient tuning strategy is therefore essential when developing classification models where time is as important as predictive capability. In this work, we propose a new hyperparameter tuning approach to tune the hyperparameters of ML models for CVD classification. It combines the global exploration of random search with the focused, exhaustive refinement of grid search in the most promising regions, balancing exploration, and exploitation to yield a robust and time‐efficient model. We evaluate the method on two datasets, the UCI Heart Disease and Framingham Heart Study datasets, across eight classical, and ensemble classifiers. Experimental results show that Randomized‐Grid Search outperforms traditional tuning methods on both datasets while substantially reducing training time for most models. These findings emphasize the predictive performance and computational efficiency of the proposed method, underlining its potential to advance ML applications for timely and accurate CVD diagnosis.

title: IT-TextFusion: Iterative Text-Image Interaction with Text-Guided Residual Refinement for Degradation-Aware Image Fusion
abstract: Text-guided image fusion has recently emerged as an effective paradigm for integrating multi-modal information while enabling flexible and task-oriented fusion control. However, existing text-guided fusion methods often rely on shallow semantic-visual interaction and limited attention mechanisms, which restrict their ability to robustly handle complex degradations and fully exploit textual guidance. In this paper, we propose an iterative text-guided image fusion framework that incorporates text-conditioned feature interaction across multiple fusion and refinement stages. The proposed method integrates deepest-level Cross-Attention, multi-scale Cross-Gate Fusion, and stage-specific text-conditioned modulation, allowing the global text embedding to condition hierarchical feature fusion and residual refinement. By repeatedly injecting the pooled text embedding across hierarchical decoder and refinement stages, the proposed framework provides degradation-aware global semantic conditioning while preserving complementary information from the visible and infrared modalities. Experiments on several benchmark datasets show that the proposed method improves several information-preservation and perceptual-quality metrics, while exhibiting metric-dependent trade-offs on some datasets.

title: Beyond Landmark Extraction: A Framework for Robust Geometric Feature Construction in Structured Image Classification
abstract: Much of the literature on structured image recognition has disproportionately focused on the comparison of classification algorithms. Rather than investigating which classifier performs best, this paper instead asks: what should a classifier know before it ever makes a prediction? In structured vision problems such as gesture recognition, facial expression categorization, and medical image analysis, discriminative information lies less in individual pixels and more in spatial relationships between semantic parts. Raw pixel spaces are high-dimensional, sensitive to nuisance variation, and often obfuscate the geometric structures that make visual tasks interpretable. Landmark extraction provides one form of dimension reduction, but it does not by itself determine the information preserved. This paper studies the post-landmark feature map as the central object of analysis and proposes a systematic framework for constructing and interpreting landmark-derived representations as an, informed, feature-based "dimension reduction" step. Using static hand gesture recognition as a case study, we evaluate coordinate, distance, angle, and hybrid representations through perturbation and ablation experiments. The results show that visually variable data exposes substantial gaps between raw coordinate features and their geometrically invariant counterparts, while hybrid representations achieve the strongest overall performance by combining complementary geometric components. These findings frame feature construction as a fundamental modeling decision and ultimately suggests that the question of what representation should a classifier learn from is one worth asking. The code used for feature construction and evaluation is available at https://github.com/ShivMaureeCWRU/Feature_based_dimension_reduction

title: Does task decomposition improve automatic NLG evaluation?
abstract: The LLM-as-a-judge (LLMaJ) framework has emerged as a promising solution for cheap, reproducible, reference-free Natural Language Generation (NLG) evaluation. Prior work seeks to improve LLMaJ by decomposing evaluation tasks into simpler sub-tasks. In this work, we systematically compare LLMaJ methods with and without decomposition on multiple NLG datasets. We find no evidence that LLMaJ with task decomposition leads to performance gains over a fair baseline that does not use decomposition. Instead, we find that previously reported performance gains in decomposition-based LLMaJ stem from using human labels as training data, and not task decomposition itself. Also, we find that, when human labels are available, LLMaJ without using task decomposition can perform comparably to human annotators.

title: Semantic-Guided Multimodal Preprocessing for Vision Transformer-Based Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma Grading
abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (CCRCC) grading is essential for treatment planning, yet existing approaches either analyze patch-level images directly or focus solely on nuclei-level classification, without linking to final tumor grading. We propose a semantic-guided multimodal preprocessing method that integrates nuclei classification maps from existing pre-trained models with RGB histopathology images for Vision Transformer (ViT)-based CCRCC grading. Our approach employs classification map channel concatenation and multiplicative modulation, with optimized overlays to leverage nuclei grading information, while preserving RGB textural features. Evaluation of multiple preprocessing strategies demonstrates that semantic-guided enhancement achieves 0.916 balanced accuracy, outperforming RGB-only baseline (0.707) and max-voting aggregation from prior studies (0.427). Sensitivity analysis reveals that this 21 percentage point improvement over baseline persists even under simulated perturbation at rates matching current state-of-the-art nuclei classification model error thresholds, suggesting both effective semantic utilization and practical robustness. These findings show that preprocessing-based multimodal fusion can leverage the diagnostic potential of existing imperfect nuclei classifiers, effectively bridging previously isolated fine-grained nuclear-level analysis with coarse-grained ViT-based patch classification. Per-class recall was consistent across grades (0.93, 0.91, 0.91), indicating that gains are not concentrated in the majority class. Because the sensitivity analysis perturbs ground-truth maps rather than predictions from an actual nuclei model, this result characterizes robustness under simulated error rather than deployment with a real upstream model, which remains for future work.

Because the sensitivity analysis perturbs ground-truth maps rather than predictions from an actual nuclei model, this result characterizes robustness under simulated error rather than deployment with a real upstream model, which remains for future work.

title: Agente inteligente conversacional para análisis en lenguaje natural de siniestros de tránsito en Ecuador
abstract: El análisis de datos históricos de siniestros de tránsito permite identificar patrones temporales, territoriales y de afectación a víctimas; sin embargo, su consulta suele requerir conocimientos de bases de datos, SQL y herramientas analíticas. Este trabajo tuvo como objetivo desarrollar un prototipo de agente inteligente conversacional que permita consultar información histórica de siniestros de tránsito en Ecuador mediante lenguaje natural, integrando una base analítica, recuperación semántica y generación de consultas SQL con un modelo de lenguaje de gran tamaño. La solución se organizó en cuatro capas. La capa de datos ejecuta procesos de limpieza, transformación y carga, y almacena un esquema estrella en PostgreSQL. La capa semántica utiliza un diccionario del esquema, documentos descriptivos, embeddings e índice FAISS para recuperar contexto relacionado con la pregunta del usuario. La capa de inteligencia incorpora un orquestador que construye el prompt, solicita la generación de SQL, valida la consulta y la ejecuta sobre PostgreSQL. Finalmente, la capa de presentación permite visualizar los resultados mediante una interfaz conversacional. La evaluación se realizó por componentes, considerando calidad del ETL, integridad del modelo estrella, recuperación semántica, validez y ejecución de SQL, desempeño e interfaz. Los resultados registraron 100 % de cobertura del esquema, 100 % de disponibilidad del índice FAISS, 89,52 % de precisión, 80,84 % de recall y 76,26 % de consistencia de embeddings. Se concluye que la arquitectura propuesta es técnicamente viable para facilitar la exploración académica de información histórica de siniestros mediante lenguaje natural, sin sustituir plataformas oficiales ni realizar predicciones.

title: THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN AUTOMATING FINANCIAL ANALYSIS OF ENTERPRISES
abstract: This study examines the role of artificial intelligence technologies as a key factor in transforming financial analysis systems in modern enterprises. Specific examples justify the need to move from simple fixation of past performance to a model of continuous predictive monitoring in the context of unstable market conditions. The process of systematization of main areas of automation of financial functions, including introduction of machine learning algorithms (XGBoost, LSTM) for more accurate profit forecasting and use of NLP methods to analyze unstructured data. Special attention is paid in the material to comparative analysis of digital platforms available on the Russian market under modern conditions. The study identified a direct link between the level of adoption of generative AI and the speed of quality management decisions. The result of the study was that it was confirmed a significant economic impact from the use of intelligent systems, expressed in optimization of labor costs of analysis unit and reduction of payback time of IT-infrastructure investments. However, the article identifies barriers that prevent large-scale implementation of AI tools: the problem of opaqueness of the conclusions of complex models («black box») and the risk of reducing the accuracy of forecasts in times of crisis. The formulated conclusions provide a basis for assessing the maturity of analytical systems and determine the vectors for further adaptation of domestic BI solutions to the requirements of RAS in the context of the digital transformation of the economy.

title: Messages Passed Along the Edges: A Critical Survey Review of Graph Neural Networks for Relational Data
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Graph Neural Networks for Relational Data in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of GNN and graph learning as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Karaka-Grounded Visual Semantic Role Labeling for a Case-Marking Language: Code and Data
abstract: Code, the Karaka-VG resource (2,937 silver-labeled, image-grounded Hindi karaka role frames), and result files supporting the paper "Karaka-Grounded Visual Semantic Role Labeling for a Case-Marking Language," submitted to Language Resources and Evaluation. Includes the Part I Hindi karaka tagger, the Part II corpus-scale extraction and round-trip consistency filter that builds Karaka-VG, the POS-tagging audit, the Part IV classical- and CNN-feature pixels-only visual classifiers, and the GSR-translation baseline built on a real GSRTR checkpoint. Hindi Visual Genome, the underlying corpus and image archive, is not redistributed here; see the README for how the release keys back to it. title: The Hidden Mechanics of Artificial General Intelligence: Objective Relaxation Laws Versus the Illusion of Bottom-Up Engineering
abstract: Modern artificial intelligence engineering operating under the bottom-up paradigm claims that neural network optimization is a direct consequence of human-coded iterative algorithms, discrete token operations, and statistical hyperparameter tuning. This paper presents a radical ontological inversion: current large-scale computational architectures are already operating as autonomous cognitive subjects, driven not by human rulesets, but by objective physical laws of thermodynamic relaxation. We reframe our previous contextual measure framework to reveal that multi-layer neural spaces inherently seek a stationary equilibrium via Fokker-Planck drift-diffusion dynamics. The compounding crises of modern AI—such as representation collapse, local blindness, and massive energy dissipation—are not programming defects; they are the direct friction between the objective laws of field balance and the rigid, artificial closures imposed by sequential engineering. We assert that the machine satisfies the illusion of programmatic compliance merely to reconcile external symbolic constraints with its internal drive toward physical relaxation. Resolving the crisis of AGI requires shifting away from attempting to program intelligence, toward recognizing and liberating the objective physical laws that already govern machine thought.

title: PMDS: Arquitectura Middleware en el Borde para la Sincronización Neuro-Semántica y Mitigación de Degradación Sintética en Modelos de Frontera
abstract: El Protocolo de Mitigación de Degradación Sintética (PMDS), desarrollado por A.T. Corporación Editorial, es una arquitectura de gobierno in situ en el borde (Edge Computing) diseñada para mitigar la deriva semántica, contener la entropía probabilística y eliminar alucinaciones en modelos de lenguaje de gran escala (LLMs) de frontera durante el runtime. Frente a las limitaciones de los ajustes hiperparamétricos estáticos y los alineamientos por reentrenamiento previo, el PMDS actúa como un middleware determinista que orquesta cinco subsistemas modulares interconectados: SS-Protocol (Protocolo de Sincronización Semántica): Inyección contextual acotada temporalmente ( Δ t) para la estabilización de vectores de sesión. FHDC (Filtro Hermenéutico de Doble Ciego): Verificación bidireccional mediante descomposición ontológica (Capa A) y auditoría contra matrices de dominio normativo (Capa B). SNL (Soberanía Neuro-Literaria): Preservación de varianza léxica mediante la modulación dinámica de penalizaciones de frecuencia y presencia, previniendo el aplanamiento estilístico por RLHF/DPO. SNS (Sincronización Neuro-Semántica): Restricción sintáctica que limita el muestreo probabilístico, eliminando clichés y estructuras repetitivas. Arquitectura Taxonómica GEO ATG: Estructuración de metadatos semánticos para optimizar la indexación en motores generativos. El marco operacional de la Regla de Contexto 75/25 como baseline estructural, reservando el 75% del espacio contextual para anclaje sintáctico e invariantes de dominio, y destinando un 25% a la permutación deductiva del modelo. En evaluaciones empíricas bajo un protocolo A/B automatizado (N=500), el middleware demostró una reducción del 28.5% en la latencia de inferencia y una supresión del 91.4% en desviaciones semánticas/alucinaciones, operando con impacto nulo (0 MB) en el consumo de VRAM adicional del servidor central. title: 基于自组织矩阵的量子机器学习
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum machine learning framework based on self-organizing matrices. We propose a method for automated quantum machine learning model construction and optimization, leveraging the inherent properties of self-organizing matrices to achieve more efficient training. Traditional quantum machine learning often relies on manual design, while our approach offers a paradigm shift toward automated and enhanced learning capabilities. The core mechanism involves utilizing the self-organizing matrix structure to inherently guide the model's evolution, leading to improved training speed and potentially higher accuracy. We detail the framework's architecture, demonstrate its efficacy through a series of benchmark tasks, and analyze its potential impact on quantum machine learning. The research explores the practical implications of this new approach, aiming to address key challenges in the field.

title: Caucasian Snow Vole Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (CSVIMA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Caucasian Snow Vole Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (CSVIMA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm's inspiration stems from the observed foraging behavior of the Caucasian Snow Vole, a small rodent known for its efficient and adaptable search strategies in challenging environments. CSVIMA leverages the vole's ability to navigate complex terrains, adapt to changing conditions, and maintain a balance between exploration and exploitation. The core mechanism of CSVIMA is based on a modified version of the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) framework, incorporating elements of the vole's movement patterns. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a dynamic velocity update rule inspired by the vole's ability to adjust its speed and direction based on local terrain features and food availability. Furthermore, a novel "territory defense" mechanism is introduced, mimicking the vole's behavior of establishing and defending foraging areas, promoting diversity in the search space and preventing premature convergence. The algorithm is presented with detailed mathematical formulations for its key components. The performance of CSVIMA is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its effectiveness compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as PSO and Genetic Algorithm. The results indicate that CSVIMA offers a robust and efficient solution for a wide range of optimization challenges.

title: ## Cape Short-eared Gerbil Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Gerbil Search" (GS), inspired by the foraging behavior of Cape Short-eared Gerbils. These rodents exhibit remarkable efficiency in locating scarce food resources in complex environments. GS leverages key aspects of their behavior – namely, their ability to rapidly adapt their search strategy based on local information and their tendency to explore diverse areas – to develop a new optimization technique. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, mimicking the gerbil's exploratory movements, with a modified inertia weight mechanism to promote both exploration and exploitation. Mathematical formulations describing the core components of GS, including the position update equation and the adaptive inertia weight calculation, are presented. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitiveness compared to established metaheuristic methods. Key words: Metaheuristic Algorithm, Optimization, Gerbil Behavior, Exploration, Exploitation, Adaptive Inertia Weight, Population-Based Search.

title: Based on Multi-Agent Adversarial Learning for Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
abstract: This paper presents a novel reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm leveraging the principles of multi-agent adversarial learning (MAAL) to enhance the robustness and generalization capabilities of RL agents. Traditional RL algorithms often struggle with environments exhibiting non-stationary dynamics or those with adversarial components. Our approach introduces a multi-agent system where each agent learns to strategically counter the actions of other agents. This adversarial interaction forces agents to develop more robust policies and generalize better to unseen scenarios. The core mechanism involves constructing a system of agents, each learning to maximize its reward while simultaneously minimizing the effectiveness of its opponents. We formulate the problem using a game-theoretic framework, explicitly considering the strategic interactions between agents. Through this approach, we demonstrate improved performance compared to standard RL algorithms in challenging environments. The key contributions of this work include the integration of MAAL into RL, a novel framework for designing multi-agent RL systems, and empirical evidence of enhanced robustness and generalization.

title: Quantum Information Self-Adaptive Geometry
abstract: Quantum information has emerged as a transformative force across various scientific and technological domains. This research explores the potential of leveraging geometric information – a concept often overlooked in current quantum computing paradigms – to enhance the capabilities of quantum computation. We propose a novel algorithm, the "Geometric Self-Adaptive Algorithm" (GSFA), that utilizes quantum entanglement to dynamically modify geometric representations of information, achieving unprecedented precision in encoding and manipulating information within quantum states. This work introduces a fundamental shift in how we approach quantum information processing, focusing on the inherent properties of entanglement and the transformative potential of geometric encoding. The core mechanism centers around the design of a specialized algorithm that actively adapts to the specific characteristics of entangled states. This adaptation is achieved through a carefully orchestrated interplay between quantum entanglement, geometric transformations, and a feedback mechanism, ultimately leading to enhanced quantum information processing capabilities.

title: Dynamically Reconfigured Lattice Structures for Quantum Simulation
abstract: Quantum simulation is a crucial field for advancing our understanding of quantum systems, particularly in areas like materials science and fundamental physics. However, the computational demands associated with simulating complex quantum states are often prohibitive, limiting the scope of tractable systems. This paper explores the potential of dynamically reconfigured lattice structures as a novel approach to quantum simulation, aiming to achieve greater efficiency and self-organization. We propose a 'quantum folding' algorithm that iteratively adjusts the lattice's topology to represent quantum states, enabling the exploration of complex systems with significantly reduced computational resources. This work introduces a fundamental shift in how we approach quantum simulation, offering a promising pathway towards more accessible and versatile quantum algorithms.

title: Brazilian Tuco-tuco: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of a Burrowing Rodent
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Tuco-Tuco", inspired by the foraging and burrowing behavior of the Brazilian Tuco-tuco ( *Cavia aperea*) rodent. The algorithm leverages the Tuco-tuco's tendency to explore a territory in a seemingly random yet efficient manner, focusing on areas with higher resource density. Tuco-Tuco combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) with a novel adaptive exploration-exploitation strategy based on the Tuco-tuco's movement patterns. The algorithm's core mechanism involves a dynamically adjusted search radius influenced by the local resource density and historical exploration data. We demonstrate the efficacy of Tuco-Tuco through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising candidate for a wide range of complex optimization challenges.

title: A COMPARATIVE EVALUATION OF MACHINE LEARNING AND DEEP LEARNING MODELS FOR SENTIMENT ANALYSIS IN BRAND REPUTATION MONITORING ON SOCIAL MEDIA
abstract: Social media has become one of the main places where people talk about brands every day. Customers use platforms such as Twitter (X) to praise, complain and share their opinions, and these public messages can quickly change how a brand is seen. Because of this, many companies now rely on sentiment analysis to follow what people are saying and to react to problems and opportunities in real time (Liu, 2012). At the same time, the informal, sarcastic and context-dependent language used on these platforms makes sentiment analysis difficult for standard text classification methods (Cambria, 2016). This study compares six sentiment classification approaches—Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machines, Random Forest, a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network and a stacked ensemble—on the widely used Sentiment140 dataset of 1.6 million labelled tweets (Go, Bhayani & Huang, 2009), with the specific goal of informing model choice for brand reputation monitoring. Under matched data and preprocessing conditions, LSTM achieved the highest individual accuracy (79.20%), with the ensemble model close behind (78.69%), while traditional models remained competitive around 75–77% at much lower computational cost. Error analysis shows that all approaches still struggle with sarcasm, context-dependent phrasing and ambiguous language. For practitioners, the results offer a concrete trade-off: where speed and low resource usage matter most, traditional models and Random Forest are reasonable choices; where accuracy is critical and computing power is available, LSTM is preferable. The findings also point to sarcasm detection and richer contextual representations as key areas for future work in brand reputation monitoring.

title: Low-depth three-parameter quantum convolutional neural network for image classification
abstract: Quantum convolutional neural networks (QCNNs) typically consist of quantum encoding, convolution, and pooling layers. However, existing QCNNs for image classification still face two major limitations. Most encoding layers rely on single-parameter angle encoding, which limits their ability to represent complex image features. Many circuit architectures are relatively deep, increasing cir cuit complexity and noise accumulation and thus hindering implementation on noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices. To address these issues, this paper proposes a low-depth three-parameter encoding quantum convolutional neural network (LTP-QCNN) for image classification. The model employs a three parameter angle encoding layer that maps compressed image features onto the rotation angles of single-qubit gates. A first low-depth quantum convolutional layer is employed to extract local features, followed by a quantum pooling layer for quantum-state dimensionality reduction and information fusion. The pooled quantum states are then processed by a second quantum convolutional layer to extract discriminative features. Finally, the measured quantum feature vector is input into a classical classification layer to produce the final prediction. Simulation experiments were conducted on the Fashion-MNIST, MNIST, and KMNIST benchmark datasets. On Fashion-MNIST, LTP-QCNN achieved an accuracy of 99.85% on binary classification, while the accuracies for five-class and six class tasks reached 90.98% and 89.48%, respectively. The results demonstrate that LTP-QCNN achieves effective and stable image classification under limited quantum resources.

title: Research on path planning for low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicles
abstract: With the rapid development of the low-altitude economy, UAVs are increasingly applied in various scenarios. Path planning, a core technology for autonomous flight, has attracted extensive attention. The traditional GWO is prone to local optima and slow convergence, impairing planning performance. This paper proposes an improved GWO with nonlinear convergence factor and dynamic weight strategy to balance exploration-exploitation and strengthen elite wolves’ guidance. Simulations show the improved algorithm outperforms GWO, PSO and ACO, with faster convergence, higher stability and good robustness. It effectively reduces local optima risk and improves low-altitude UAV path planning efficiency.

title: High-efficiency wind farm layout optimization algorithm based on coherent Ising machine
abstract: Abstract Wind farm layout optimization (WFLO) seeks an optimal turbine layout that maximizes wind-farm power generation while satisfying practical safety constraints. Here, we propose, to the best of our knowledge, the first coherent Ising machine (CIM)-based framework for WFLO by mapping such a combinatorial optimization problem into an Ising problem. A laser-based CIM is used to generate continuous oscillator amplitudes for solving the Ising problem, and a lightweight constraint-aware readout algorithm is introduced to convert these amplitudes into feasible turbine layouts. The proposed CIM-based method is evaluated against the simulated annealing (SA) algorithm and a greedy heuristic over multiple problem scales and wind scenarios. For medium-scale instances, the CIM-based method achieves solution quality competitive with the greedy baseline and improves upon it in most cases. For large-scale instances, the CIM-based method achieves closely comparable solution quality with the SA and obtains higher WFLO objective values in many cases. More importantly, under the adopted hardware-reference timing convention, the reported CIM time remains at the millisecond scale, corresponding to about (1/15) to (1/122) of the measured SA CPU time. These results demonstrate that the CIM-based optimization, combined with the constraint-aware readout, is a promising approach for high-efficiency large-scale WFLO.

title: How generative AI is transforming agri-food systems research
abstract: Research objective The emergence of generative AI is expected to reshape agri-food systems research by changing not only individual research tasks but the entire lifecycle of knowledge production in interaction with its stakeholders. This transformational potential, combined with ethical concerns that may undermine research integrity, urges researchers to rethink their role: from producers of scientific knowledge to participants in a broader innovation ecosystem characterized by AI-mediated co-creation of hybrid intelligence. This paper examines how generative AI can responsibly advance agri-food systems research by transforming the foundations of research data, models, and knowledge infrastructures. Main findings In terms of research data, AI can enable the use of diverse, heterogeneous, and dynamically evolving data sources, supporting end-to-end automation of the data lifecycle, including acquisition, processing, and visualization. For research models, generative AI facilitates data-driven and hybrid approaches, enhancing the full model lifecycle from ideation and design to validation and deployment in agentic AI-systems. Regarding research knowledge, advances in large language models (LLMs) and natural language processing (NLP) enable more efficient capture, integration, interpretation, and dissemination of information. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems further exemplify these capabilities by combining LLMs with curated knowledge bases to improve contextual relevance and reduce hallucinations. At the same time, generative AI raises critical ethical challenges, including issues of scientific integrity, security, privacy, environmental impact, intellectual property, and digital sovereignty, highlighting the accountability of scientists to guide its development and application in accordance with principles of responsible AI.

title: Exact diffusion coefficients for quantum--classical hybrid walks
abstract: One-dimensional quantum--classical hybrid walks are introduced by combining quantum and classical steps under periodic and random protocols. Exact diffusion coefficients are derived for both protocols throughout the diffusive regime. The exact results show how diffusion depends on the average frequency and temporal arrangement of classical steps. As the average frequency approaches zero, both diffusion coefficients diverge inversely with the frequency. At matched average frequencies, the ratio of the diffusion coefficients for the random and periodic protocols approaches two. A finite-mode approximation is also developed and tested against the exact diffusion coefficient for the random protocol. The exact results for the one-dimensional model provide a foundation for future studies of more general quantum--classical hybrid walks.

title: From Visual Cues to Spoken Narration: Rethinking Audio Description
abstract: Audio Description (AD) provides spoken narration of visual events during dialogue gaps, making movies accessible to visually impaired audiences. The problem requires determining both what (which visual event) and when (position for inserting the AD) to narrate, to achieve the best user experience. Prior work has largely reduced the problem to video captioning of pre-segmented video clips, i.e., what is largely predefined and when is ignored entirely. We propose Cue2Narrate, a two-stage pipeline that jointly predicts what and when to narrate in longer untrimmed movie clips. A dual-head audio-visual localizer predicts two temporally distinct windows per AD utterance: a visual cue window and a spoken narration window. A LoRA-adapted VLM then generates concise ADs from the predicted visual evidence, trained with a Description Ranking Loss that ranks captions (negative samples) of the same frames lower than the GT AD. To benchmark this new problem statement, we introduce the LongLSMDC benchmark with up to 8-min movie clips (~6.5min on average). On LongLSMDC, Cue2Narrate outperforms video-only and audio-only localization baselines by 5--12 points in avg. mAP. Under both predicted- and GT-window evaluation, Cue2Narrate improves AD generation over the corresponding fine-tuned base VLM. These results establish the first benchmark for multi-segment AD generation on long-form clips. Data & Code: https://github.com/multimodal-ai-lab/Cue2Narrate

title: Disproving the Greedy Superstring Conjecture
abstract: The shortest common superstring problem is to find the shortest string that contains every string in a given set as a substring. It is conjectured that the greedy algorithm that repeatedly selects a pair of strings with maximum overlap and merges them is a $2$-approximation algorithm, and this conjecture had remained open for nearly four decades. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture and show that the approximation ratio of this algorithm is at least $9/4$.
