title: Where the Verifier Fails: A Category-Level Audit of Reward Signals in RLVR
abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) and standard benchmark evaluation both rely on an automatic verifier that turns a free text answer into a binary reward. Prior work reports that one evaluation harness accepts only about 94% of its own ground truth answers, blaming LaTeX parsing. That is an aggregate: it does not say which answer forms consume the error budget. We supply the decomposition. We apply metamorphic testing to the verifier rather than the model, generating certified equivalent answer variants, that is, rewrites that preserve mathematical meaning by construction, so that any rejection is a provable false negative needing no human adjudication. We then measure rejection per answer category across four widely used verifiers over 307,420 verdicts. We find three things. (1) Self validation ranges from 53.8% to 95.2% on identical inputs, a spread of 41.3 points. The published figure describes one implementation, not the task; two configurations of the same library disagree on 49.9% of pairs. (2) The residual is not spread across parsing categories but concentrated in whitespace and punctuation, which account for 93.0% of in contract failures for the default LaTeX configuration. A trailing period or newline dominates the budget. (3) Separating rejection from execution failure shows that verifiers with similar aggregate error fail for opposite reasons, and that a reference numeric cascade accepts off by one wrong answers as a step function of magnitude, from 0% below 10^4 to 100% at or above, because its relative tolerance is scale invariant.

title: List Size of Random Linear Codes: Optimality and the Limits of Average-Radius List Decoding
abstract: Guruswami, Li, Mosheiff, Resch, Silas and Wootters conjectured that, for every fixed prime power $q$ and $p\in(0,1-1/q)$, random linear codes of rate $1-h_q(p)-\varepsilon$ have list size $\frac{h_q(p)}{\varepsilon}\cdot(1+o(1))$ as $\varepsilon\to0$, both for list decoding and average-radius list decoding. The conjecture was known for $q=2$ and remained open for larger alphabets. We prove the conjecture for list decoding for every prime power $q$, with the sharper bound $L=\frac{h_q(p)}{\varepsilon}+O_{p,q}(1).$ In contrast, we disprove the conjecture for average-radius list decoding. We show that the required list-size leading constant is at least $p\left(1+\log_q\frac{(q-1)(1-p)}{p}\right)$, which is strictly larger than $h_q(p)$ whenever $q^p(1-p)>1$. Moreover, for $p=1-λ/q$ with fixed $λ>1$, the required leading constant can be as large as $\left(\frac{\logλ}{eλ}+o_q(1)\right)\frac{q}{\log q}.$

title: A Checklist to assess the energy and carbon impacts of ML/AI applications in Earth System Modeling
abstract: As machine learning and artificial intelligence find their way into nearly every aspect of climate, weather, and Earth system modeling, it is worth pausing to consider what our design decisions imply for the science and for the computational resources we consume. A growing body of literature addresses the ethical and sustainable development of ML/AI, yet translating these principles into day-to-day research practice remains a challenge as most of best practices are dispersed across multiple studies and commentaries. Here, we distill these discussions into a practical checklist that ML/AI and Earth system science practitioners can use to assess and reduce the environmental footprint of their own applications, organised around the successive stages of the model development pipeline. We complement the checklist with a selection of metrics drawn from the literature for estimating the energy consumption and carbon footprint of a project. For each question, we point to concrete examples and actionable suggestions from recent literature, aiming to bridge the gap between aspirational principles and the decisions researchers face at every stage of the development cycle.

title: Leveraging Cloud Computing and Big Data Analytics to Enhance Ideological Education Platforms in Universities
abstract: Education is going through a remarkable transformation brought about by the convergence of cloud computing and big data, which have enabled educational institutions to develop very different and individualized learning experiences for each student depending on his/her needs. But, even with the technology in place, the tracking of engagement in ideological education has not been able to break its limitations, causing disengagement, which is consequently leading to slow overall learning. The authors of the paper propose to create a flexible and tolerant cloud-based educational platform using big data analytics powered by AI in the Higher Education sector. One of the main goals of the research is to establish a system that will employ AI for the real-time classification of student engagement based on EEG signals and behavioral data and will thus adapt the content and the learning paths accordingly. The investigation will utilize a combination of Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and Long Short-Term Memory networks (LSTM) African Vultures Optimization Algori thm (AVOA) will be used for feature selection, and cloud-based data storage will be provided to make the system scalable. The performance results of the proposed system have shown a very significant improvement over traditional models, with the MLP-LSTM combination achieving an accuracy of 92.6%, precision of 92.1%, recall of 91.8%, and F1 score of 91.9%.

evidence.abstract: Education is going through a remarkable transformation brought about by the convergence of cloud computing and big data, which have enabled educational institutions to develop very different and individualized learning experiences for each student depending on his/her needs. But, even with the technology in place, the tracking of engagement in ideological education has not been able to break its limitations, causing disengagement, which is consequently leading to slow overall learning. The authors of the paper propose to create a flexible and tolerant cloud-based educational platform using big data analytics powered by AI in the Higher Education sector. One of the main goals of the research is to establish a system that will employ AI for the real-time classification of student engagement based on EEG signals and behavioral data and will thus adapt the content and the learning paths accordingly. The investigation will utilize a combination of Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and Long Short-Term Memory networks (LSTM) African Vultures Optimization Algori thm (AVOA) will be used for feature selection, and cloud-based data storage will be provided to make the system scalable. The performance results of the proposed system have shown a very significant improvement over traditional models, with the MLP-LSTM combination achieving an accuracy of 92.6%, precision of 92.1%, recall of 91.8%, and F1 score of 91.9%.

title: Bigger, Better, or Just Bigger: A Contemporary Synthesis Review of The Scaling Laws Debate in Modern Machine Learning
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of The Scaling Laws Debate in Modern Machine Learning in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of scaling laws and compute as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Chapman's Rice Rat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Oryzomys spp.*
abstract: This paper presents Chapman's Rice Rat (CRR), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging strategies of *Oryzomys spp.* (Chapman's rice rats). These rodents are renowned for their efficient and adaptable foraging behavior, particularly their ability to exploit patchy environments with limited information. CRR leverages these observed traits to develop a new optimization approach. The algorithm utilizes a dynamic population of potential solutions, represented as vectors, and employs a novel "patch exploration" mechanism mimicking the rice rat's movement pattern. A key component is a 'memory' system that tracks the rat's recent foraging locations, biasing subsequent movements towards areas with higher potential rewards. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations on various benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its efficacy in finding near-optimal solutions with reasonable computational cost. Specifically, we examine CRR's performance on the Rastrigin, Sphere, and Brent test functions, highlighting its strengths in escaping local optima and its ability to converge to solutions with good fitness values. The algorithm's parameters are tuned using a grid search method, optimizing the balance between exploration and exploitation. Future research directions include incorporating more complex environmental modeling and exploring the application of CRR to real-world engineering and scientific problems.

title: Distributed Differential Privacy via Lagrangian Relaxation of Network Flow
abstract: Achieving robust differential privacy guarantees in distributed network flow computations presents a significant challenge. Traditional approaches often suffer from substantial information loss during aggregation, leading to weakened privacy protections. This paper introduces a novel framework that leverages Lagrangian relaxation to address this issue. We reformulate the privacy-preserving network flow problem by incorporating Lagrange multipliers, which directly represent the privacy constraints. These multipliers are dynamically adjusted through distributed optimization, balancing privacy preservation with flow accuracy. This dynamic adjustment process is key to mitigating the information loss inherent in distributed aggregation. The proposed method offers a practical and effective solution for achieving strong differential privacy in distributed network flow scenarios, contributing to the growing field of privacy-aware distributed computing. Our approach avoids the pitfalls of naive aggregation and provides a more nuanced control over the privacy-utility trade-off. The core contribution is the dynamic adjustment of Lagrange multipliers, a technique that allows for a more efficient and accurate privacy-preserving network flow computation. ---

title: 基于非线性模型的深度学习的自适应学习策略
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive learning strategy based on non-linear models for deep learning, leveraging dynamic adjustment of learning rate and regularization parameters to enhance model generalization. Traditional deep learning methods often employ fixed parameters, aiming to improve generalization. Our approach dynamically adjusts these parameters to optimize performance across diverse datasets. We present a framework that effectively mitigates overfitting and accelerates convergence, resulting in improved model robustness and generalization capabilities. The core mechanism involves the utilization of non-linear models for learning, coupled with a sophisticated adaptive control system for parameter tuning. This work addresses the limitations of existing approaches by providing a more flexible and robust method for self-optimizing deep learning models.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Topological Mapping
abstract: Quantum-enhanced topological mapping seeks to revolutionize the study of complex topological structures by employing quantum algorithms to facilitate exploration and analysis. This paper investigates the potential of quantum tunneling and superposition to uncover hidden relationships and patterns within these structures, offering a novel approach to deeper understanding. We outline the core mechanism, detailing how quantum phenomena can accelerate and enhance the detection of topological invariants, potentially surpassing the limitations of classical techniques. The investigation will focus on leveraging quantum algorithms to map and analyze topological landscapes, offering a pathway to fundamentally alter our comprehension of these fundamental materials. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future research directions.

title: ## Brukkaros Pygmy Rock Mouse-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BPMRA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Brukkaros Pygmy Rock Mouse-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BPMRA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Brukkaros pygmy rock mice* (Trilocularietta spp.) found in the Kalahari Desert. These mice exhibit remarkable efficiency in locating scarce food resources, demonstrating a complex interplay of exploration and exploitation strategies. BPMRA leverages these principles through a dynamically adjusted adaptive search mechanism, a novel mutation operator, and a unique convergence criterion. The algorithm's core components, including the resource distribution, movement strategy, and decision-making process, are meticulously designed to mimic the observed behavior of the mice. The algorithm is demonstrated through several benchmark problems, showcasing its effectiveness in solving continuous and combinatorial optimization problems. The results indicate that BPMRA provides a competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms like Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Future work will focus on further refining the algorithm's parameters and exploring its applicability to more complex and real-world optimization challenges.

title: Title: Non-Standard Geometry for Parallel Machine Learning
abstract: This paper explores the application of non-standard geometry as a novel representation for parallel machine learning. The inherent properties of geometric structures, such as symmetry and redundancy, offer a potential advantage over traditional linear algebra-based approaches. We propose a new geometric framework that is specifically designed to be efficiently parallelized, aiming to accelerate the training process for machine learning models. The core mechanism focuses on leveraging geometric transformations and representations to improve computational efficiency, thereby addressing a significant bottleneck in current machine learning methodologies. This research investigates the potential benefits of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimentation. The goal is to demonstrate a significant improvement in training time compared to existing methods, particularly when dealing with large datasets and complex models.

title: Adaptive Domain Self-Correlation
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative algorithm, Adaptive Domain Self-Correlation, designed to enhance the generalization and efficiency of machine learning models through dynamic weight adjustment based on domain self-correlation. Traditional feature selection and optimization methods primarily focus on feature selection, while this approach leverages the inherent self-correlation within datasets to dynamically adjust model parameters. The core mechanism involves quantifying and leveraging this self-correlation to reduce model parameter redundancy and improve adaptability. We present a novel framework that systematically assesses and utilizes domain self-correlation to guide weight optimization, resulting in a more robust and efficient model. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of this method through a series of experiments comparing it to existing techniques.

title: Causal Discovery from High-Dimensional Observational Data via Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for causal discovery from high-dimensional observational data leveraging Bayesian Networks. The core challenge in causal discovery is the "curse of dimensionality," where the complexity of the data rapidly increases with the number of variables, leading to inaccurate and incomplete causal graphs. Existing algorithms frequently fail to scale effectively or introduce significant biases in high-dimensional settings. Our approach incorporates prior knowledge through expert-defined constraints and utilizes regularization techniques to mitigate the impact of noise and redundancy. The algorithm iteratively refines a Bayesian Network structure by evaluating conditional independence tests, incorporating prior probabilities, and applying a penalty term that favors simpler, more parsimonious graphs. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the method through theoretical analysis and illustrative examples, highlighting its ability to generate more reliable causal structures compared to traditional methods in high-dimensional scenarios. The key contribution lies in a robust framework that balances exploration of potential causal relationships with the need for structural simplicity, ultimately providing a more accurate representation of the underlying causal mechanisms.

title: ## Black-tailed Woodrat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Woodrat Search" (WS), inspired by the foraging behavior of the black-tailed woodrat. Woodrats are known for their efficient and adaptive strategies for locating and securing food resources in complex environments. The WS algorithm leverages these behaviors – specifically, the combination of systematic exploration and opportunistic exploitation – to address complex optimization problems. The core of the WS algorithm utilizes a population of potential solutions, each represented by a vector of parameters. Movement within the search space is governed by a probabilistic mechanism mimicking the woodrat's exploration and caching patterns. A key component is the "Cache" mechanism, which simulates the woodrat's ability to remember and revisit promising locations. The algorithm employs a dynamic weight parameter to balance exploration and exploitation, adapting to the characteristics of the problem being solved. The performance of the WS algorithm is evaluated on a range of benchmark functions, demonstrating its competitive effectiveness compared to established metaheuristic methods such as the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Genetic Algorithm (GA). The algorithm's adaptability and efficient use of search space make it a promising approach for a variety of optimization challenges.

title: MSGSO: A Multi-Strategy Glider Snake Optimizer for Global Optimization and 3D UAV Path Planning
abstract: Information in the Glider Snake Optimizer (GSO) propagates through a leader-predecessor chain. This structure is simple, but it can lose diversity when adjacent agents converge to the same region. The proposed Multi-Strategy Glider Snake Optimizer (MSGSO) retains the original GSO update and subsequently applies nonlinear dynamic polynomial mutation (NDM), elite opposition-based learning (EOBL), and quadratic interpolation (QI). MSGSO was evaluated on CEC 2019 and CEC 2022 with 30 matched random seeds and 15,000 objective evaluations for every algorithm-problem pair. The experiments included seven alternative optimizers and all single, pairwise, and three-operator GSO variants. Across the 34 benchmark problems, MSGSO significantly outperformed GSO on 31 and showed no significant loss. It nevertheless ranked third in each external comparison: L-SHADE led CEC 2019 and CEC 2022 at D=10, while CMA-ES led CEC 2022 at D=20. The ablation attributed most of the gain to NDM; NDM-GSO led the GSO variants on CEC 2019, and NDM-QI-GSO led at both CEC 2022 dimensions. In the UAV study, MSGSO returned 29 feasible paths in 30 runs in Scenario 1 and feasible paths in every run in the other two scenarios. It led the feasibility-first ranking in Scenarios 1 and 2 and placed third in Scenario 3. Thus, MSGSO improves its parent algorithm, although the full three-operator sequence is not consistently the best configuration.

title: Tra immaginazione e funzione. Ecologie educative e costruzione degli immaginari robotici a scuola
abstract: Il contributo esplora gli immaginari sui robot di bambini e preadolescenti coinvolti in percorsi PNRR di coding e robotica educativa. Sono state raccolte 753 produzioni (testuali e grafiche) in risposta alla domanda aperta "Che cos'è per te un robot?", analizzate attraverso un approccio di reflexive thematic analysis integrato da analisi descrittive e inferenziali. I risultati evidenziano una distribuzione non casuale delle rappresentazioni lungo il percorso scolastico, con una traiettoria che va da forme iconiche e non stabilizzate nelle classi iniziali, a rappresentazioni mediate dai repertori culturali nel passaggio verso la secondaria, fino a definizioni più ontologiche e funzionali al termine di quest'ultima. La categoria più frequente riguarda la natura del robot, mentre risultano meno sviluppate le dimensioni relazionali ed etiche. Lo studio suggerisce di considerare gli immaginari come risorse epistemiche situate e invita a progettare percorsi di robotica educativa che integrino dimensione tecnica, critica e valoriale.

title: AI Hallucination in Financial Research
abstract: This article examines the risk of hallucination when using large language models (LLMs) for financial research and demonstrates the unreliability of off-the-shelf tools such as ChatGPT for tasks requiring precise financial reasoning. A simple, replicable experiment was conducted using the free online version of ChatGPT-4o. The same prompt concerning capital budgeting studies advocating dual discount rates for cash inflows and outflows was submitted on three consecutive days to assess the consistency and accuracy of the model’s responses. The results reveal extensive fabrication of academic references and significant logical inconsistency. Approximately half of the cited studies were fictitious and could not be verified. In addition, the model produced contradictory responses regarding the appropriate discount rates for different cash flows, with its recommendations reversing across days. These findings provide further evidence that off-the-shelf LLMs remain unreliable for precise financial applications and highlight the need for careful use and independent verification by researchers.

evidence.title: AI Hallucination in Financial Research
evidence.abstract: This article examines the risk of hallucination when using large language models (LLMs) for financial research and demonstrates the unreliability of off-the-shelf tools such as ChatGPT for tasks requiring precise financial reasoning. A simple, replicable experiment was conducted using the free online version of ChatGPT-4o. The same prompt concerning capital budgeting studies advocating dual discount rates for cash inflows and outflows was submitted on three consecutive days to assess the consistency and accuracy of the model’s responses. The results reveal extensive fabrication of academic references and significant logical inconsistency. Approximately half of the cited studies were fictitious and could not be verified. In addition, the model produced contradictory responses regarding the appropriate discount rates for different cash flows, with its recommendations reversing across days. These findings provide further evidence that off-the-shelf LLMs remain unreliable for precise financial applications and highlight the need for careful use and independent verification by researchers.

title: PENERAPAN APLIKASI DOMPET DIGITAL BERBASIS NFC DENGAN DETEKSI FRAUD Z-SCORE
authors: Hayat, Muhyiddin A.M.; Informatika /Fakultas Teknik, Universitas Muhammadiyah Makassar
Hijrah, Hijrah; Informatika /Fakultas Teknik, Universitas Muhammadiyah Makassar
abstract: Near Field Communication (NFC) memungkinkan pembayaran nirkontak dilakukan secara cepat dan praktis, tetapi penerapannya pada dompet digital tetap membutuhkan mekanisme keamanan yang mampu mengenali transaksi tidak wajar selama proses pembayaran berlangsung. Penelitian ini mengimplementasikan aplikasi dompet digital berbasis NFC yang terintegrasi dengan Z-Score Based Anomaly Detection sebagai mekanisme deteksi fraud secara real-time. Sistem dikembangkan menggunakan React Native dan Expo Dev Client pada aplikasi mobile, Node.js dan Express.js pada backend, SQLite melalui Prisma ORM sebagai penyimpanan data, serta dashboard admin berbasis web untuk pemantauan. Proses deteksi fraud dilakukan dengan membandingkan transaksi baru terhadap dua puluh transaksi historis terakhir setiap pengguna. Nilai mean dan standar deviasi sampel dihitung dari baseline historis, kemudian nilai Z-Score digunakan untuk menentukan keputusan ALLOW, REVIEW, atau BLOCK. Pengujian dilakukan melalui simulasi manual, pengujian fungsional, pengujian keamanan, dan pengujian kompatibilitas perangkat Android. Hasil simulasi menunjukkan bahwa sistem mampu membedakan transaksi normal, mencurigakan, dan anomali. Andri memperoleh keputusan ALLOW dengan Z = 1,4142, Ibnu memperoleh REVIEW dengan Z = 2,6333, dan Adit memperoleh BLOCK dengan Z = 5,0332. Sistem juga mampu menangani kondisi khusus σ = 0 dengan mengizinkan transaksi identik dan memblokir transaksi yang berbeda dari pola historis. Hasil ini menunjukkan bahwa metode yang diterapkan ringan, transparan, dan relevan untuk keamanan pembayaran NFC pada tingkat prototipe.

title: Discrete Evolutionary Algorithm with Distance-Based Crossover and Multiple Mutation Strategy for Traveling Salesman Problems
abstract: The Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) is a fundamental combinatorial optimization problem for which traditional evolutionary algorithms often converge prematurely and yield suboptimal solutions as problem complexity increases. This study aims to overcome these limitations by developing an optimization approach that maintains population diversity while accelerating convergence toward optimal routes. To address these challenges, we introduce Evolutionary Algorithm with Distance-based Crossover and Multiple Mutation Strategy (EADXMM), a novel evolutionary algorithm characterized by its unique hybrid mechanism. Unlike standard approaches, EADXMM employs a distance-based crossover operator to produce better-guided offspring and a multi-strategy mutation framework that actively preserves and enhances population diversity. Following the mutation phase, a complete 2-opt local search is executed to refine candidate solutions and ensure rapid convergence. The performance of EADXMM was rigorously evaluated on 22 benchmark TSP instances of varying scale from the TSPLIB repository and compared against four established metaheuristics: ACO, VTPSO, ABCSS, and DSMO. Experimental results demonstrate that EADXMM exhibits superior robustness and solution quality, consistently outperforming the competing algorithms on 15 of the 22 benchmark instances. These findings confirm that the strategic integration of distance-based crossover, diversified mutation methods, and complete 2-opt local search effectively navigates the complex search space, enabling highly efficient route determination for large-scale TSPs.

title: Base de datos de señales de voz en inglés con diferentes acentos
abstract: Esta base de datos contiene señales de voz de 10 hablantes masculinos que pronuncian la misma frase en inglés, representando diferentes acentos asociados con distintos países. Todas las grabaciones fueron realizadas bajo condiciones controladas utilizando el mismo dispositivo y procedimiento de adquisición. Cada archivo contiene dos repeticiones de la frase y está identificado mediante un código anónimo. La base de datos será utilizada para analizar y comparar características de las señales en los dominios del tiempo y la frecuencia, tomando el inglés norteamericano como referencia.

title: Neighborhood elite learning multi-strategy cooperative particle swarm optimization for coordinated simultaneous arrival path planning of multiple amphibious UAVs
abstract: This paper addresses the coordinated simultaneous-arrival path planning problem for multiple amphibious unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) operating under heterogeneous speed constraints in complex amphibious environments. Unlike conventional UAVs, amphibious UAVs must traverse both aerial and aquatic domains, which imposes distinct speed constraints and dynamic adaptability requirements. The objective is to generate collision-free, smooth trajectories that enable all UAVs to reach a common target simultaneously while respecting individual speed limits, avoiding terrain obstacles, and preventing inter-vehicle collisions. To solve this problem, we propose a novel algorithm, termed NEL_MSCPSO (neighborhood elite learning-based multi-strategy cooperative particle swarm optimization). The algorithm integrates hierarchical neighborhood reconstruction with cross-subswarm elite learning, weighted centroid-guided follower updates, fully adaptive parameter adjustment, a hybrid Gaussian-Cauchy mutation scheme with elite protection, adaptive dimensional mutation on the global best, and an enhanced differential evolution-based terminal replacement strategy. Comprehensive experiments on the CEC2022 benchmark suite demonstrate that NEL_MSCPSO achieves the lowest total rank sum among twelve state-of-the-art metaheuristic algorithms. Ablation studies confirm the necessity of each component. More importantly, the algorithm is successfully applied to four multi-amphibious UAV path planning scenarios of increasing spatial complexity, consistently producing feasible trajectories that strictly satisfy simultaneous-arrival constraints under heterogeneous speed profiles. These results demonstrate the superior engineering feasibility and robustness of NEL_MSCPSO for amphibious UAV coordination tasks.

title: Gaussian Processes on Directed Metric Graphs
abstract: We introduce a statistical framework for Gaussian fields indexed at arbitrary edge locations on general compact directed metric graphs. The construction is based on a stochastic differential equation with a first-order operator and conditions at the vertices. We characterise well-posedness and identify the covariance reproducing kernel Hilbert space. We also connect the proposed framework to earlier stream-network models, showing that these arise from the same system under particular boundary conditions, and introduce new boundary conditions that yield more physically realistic processes. The differential-equation representation enables computationally efficient inference and prediction. This makes the method applicable to large data sets without approximation. Applications to temperature modelling on river networks and traffic speeds on road networks illustrate the framework, including the computational efficiency and improved performance under physically informed vertex conditions.

title: SymFold: Synergizing Evolutionary and Structural Priors for Accurate Protein Inverse Folding
abstract: Protein inverse folding aims to recover amino acid sequences for a given 3D protein structure, underpinning broad applications such as enzyme engineering and drug discovery.Current methods often follow a serial pipeline, in which a structure encoder predicts a coarse sequence, which is then refined by protein language models (PLMs). However, because PLMs only perform post-hoc sequence edits, the refinement is bounded by the quality of upstream predictions.Thanks to recent multimodal protein language models (MPLMs), we could directly encode structure to generate sequences with pretrained structural knowledge, but we observe that they are not effective for inverse folding. Therefore, we introduce a symmetric dual-path architecture that both leverages PLMs for pretrained sequence evolution knowledge and MPLMs for pretrained structural knowledge to iteratively guide protein sequence generation.Through extensive experiments across standard protein inverse folding benchmarks, our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, surpassing prior approaches, and ablation studies validate the rationale of our symmetric design, revealing a promising direction for the community.

title: An Intelligent Decision Support System for Emotion Monitoring using Microscopic Fixational Dynamics
abstract: The rising prevalence of psychological disorders necessitates effective emotion monitoring, yet current methods relying on facial or physiological signals often suffer from intrusiveness and privacy issues. This paper proposes an intelligent decision support system and pervasive edge-computing framework that leverages smart glasses and a companion smartphone to infer emotional states from microscopic visual fixation patterns. Moving beyond traditional macroscopic gaze metrics, the proposed system extracts and decomposes three distinct neurophysiological micro-movements: microsaccades, ocular drifts, and ocular microtremors. We introduce an interpretable hybrid artificial intelligence pipeline combining a multi-head attention mechanism, extreme gradient boosting, and a support vector machine to extract deep temporal features, quantify their physiological importance, and perform efficient on-device classification. Through an extensive evaluation involving 60 volunteers, we rigorously validate the framework under a strict leave-one-subject-out cross-validation protocol across both controlled and naturalistic mobile scenarios. Ablation studies unequivocally demonstrate that these fixational micro-movements are substantially more discriminative for emotion inference than traditional macroscopic features. Furthermore, aligned with contemporary affective science, the system incorporates a few-shot personalization mechanism to bridge universal physiological baselines with individual emotional heterogeneity, achieving a highly robust personalized F1-score of 83.6%. This work establishes a physiologically interpretable, unobtrusive, and deployable paradigm for continuous real-time emotion monitoring.

title: ExpArt-KG: Artwork Image Description Generation through Iterative Exploration of Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) achieve strong performance on image-grounded text generation and visual question answering. However, it remains difficult for them to comprehensively and accurately describe the factual relations among the entities and concepts associated with the objects depicted in an image. In this work, we propose a framework that efficiently exploits factual information from a knowledge graph via retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), with the goal of enabling LVLMs to generate detailed and accurate image explanations. Specifically, our method alternates between answer generation and knowledge-graph retrieval, and controls the search using a correctness judgment, thereby acquiring the necessary and sufficient factual information efficiently. We also construct a knowledge graph for the artwork domain (ExpArt-KG), in which the correspondence between images and entities is unambiguous. Applying the proposed method to this knowledge graph, we show experimentally that it improves the level of detail of artwork explanations and reduces the retrieval cost of external knowledge while maintaining generation quality comparable to that of iterating a fixed number of times.

title: Measuring consistency via ensemble margin and local prediction variability: Auditing decision systems in the presence of predictive multiplicity
abstract: The Rashomon effect is a machine learning phenomenon where equally accurate models produce different predictions for the same inputs (predictive multiplicity). Existing work primarily focuses on multiplicity within individual models, but in more complex decision systems, the impact of the Rashomon effect is less well understood. In this work, we study multiplicity from the perspective of auditing incorrect ensemble predictions, where the decision to divert an instance for human review is based on a consistency criterion that combines the ensemble margin with a measure of local prediction variability for each constituent model. With mild assumptions about stability and smoothness, we show that the consistency scores of finite ensembles converge to the corresponding consistency score of the expected model from the Rashomon set as the ensemble size and the number of samples used to measure local prediction variability increase. To demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed criterion, we evaluate the framework with respect to transformer models applied to natural language understanding tasks and parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large language models used for tabular data classification tasks. Our experiments show that ensembling models from the Rashomon set substantially reduces the risk of incorrect predictions going unchecked compared with auditing a single model, while incurring only a moderate increase in the number of diversions. Moreover, the auditing behavior of the full Rashomon set can be closely approximated by finite ensembles of relatively modest size, with the risk approaching zero for some datasets. We further demonstrate that the proposed measure exhibits stronger agreement with established predictive multiplicity metrics than existing consistency measures, providing a more reliable way to capture multiplicity in the Rashomon set.

title: Explainable and adaptive machine learning for used-car valuation: a modular framework for brand effects and pricing-risk analysis
abstract: Los precios de los vehículos usados reflejan no solo sus características técnicas y de uso, sino también la percepción de la marca, las condiciones del mercado y factores que no se observan directamente. Esto dificulta la estimación de un precio justo y genera un equilibrio entre precisión predictiva, interpretabilidad y capacidad de adaptación. Esta tesis analiza si separar el valor técnico del vehículo de los efectos de marca puede constituir una alternativa útil frente a los modelos que integran directamente la información de marca, especialmente cuando aparecen marcas no vistas previamente. Se comparan tres enfoques de valoración. Un modelo técnico ciego a la marca (M1) que estima el precio sin utilizar la marca ni del modelo. Un enfoque de ajuste modular (M2) que obtiene multiplicadores suavizados de marca-modelo a partir de los residuos de M1 y los aplica sin volver a entrenar el modelo técnico. Por otra parte, un modelo sensible a la marca (M3) que incorpora directamente la marca y el modelo mediante Categorical Boosting. El marco se evalúa mediante validación cruzada, un conjunto de prueba independiente, un experimento con marcas no vistas, explicabilidad (SHAP) y un análisis del riesgo de precios basado en residuos. En el conjunto de prueba independiente, M1 alcanza un error absoluto medio (MAE) de 2.608C y un coeficiente de determinación (R2 ) de 0,900, lo que indica que las características técnicas y de uso observables explican la mayor parte de la variación de los precios anunciados. El ajuste exploratorio de M2 reduce el MAE a 2.572C, mientras que M3 obtiene el mejor rendimiento en la evaluación estándar, con un MAE de 2.267C y un R2 de 0,935. El análisis SHAP identifica la antigüedad del vehículo, el año, la potencia y el peso como los predictores más influyentes, mientras que la información de marca y modelo aporta ajustes adicionales. La clasificación de los modelos cambia para las marcas no vistas previamente. M3 obtiene un rendimiento inferior al M1, mientras que la calibración de M2 reduce el MAE de 5.098C a 3.009C sin volver a entrenar M1. Estos resultados sugieren que la integración directa de la marca es más eficaz cuando las marcas están representadas durante el entrenamiento, mientras que la calibración modular ofrece una mayor capacidad de adaptación y transparencia cuando no lo están. Además, los residuos se convierten en indicadores de riesgo de precios para priorizar desviaciones inusuales que requieran revisión humana. Por tanto, el marco debe interpretarse principalmente como un sistema de apoyo a la toma de decisiones para la valoración y revisión del inventario, y no como un mecanismo para determinar de forma definitiva si un vehículo está incorrectamente valorado. --ABSTRACT-- Used-car prices reflect not only technical and usage characteristics but also brand perception, market conditions, and factors that are not directly observed. This makes fair-price estimation difficult and creates a trade-off between predictive accuracy, interpretability, and adaptability. This thesis asks whether separating technical vehicle value from brand effects can provide a useful alternative to fully integrated brand-aware modelling, particularly when previously unseen brands enter the market. Three valuation approaches are compared. A brand-blind technical model (M1) estimates price without using brand or model identity. A modular adjustment approach (M2) derives smoothed brand-model multipliers from M1 residuals and applies them without retraining the technical model. A brand-aware model (M3) instead incorporates brand and model directly through Categorical Boosting. The framework is evaluated through cross-validation, held-out testing, an unseen-brand experiment, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and residualbased pricing-risk analysis. On the held-out test set, M1 reaches a mean absolute error (MAE) of 2,608C and a coefficient of determination (R2 ) of 0.900, indicating that observable technical and usage characteristics explain most of the variation in listing prices. The exploratory M2 adjustment reduces MAE to 2,572C, while M3 achieves the strongest standard-evaluation performance with an MAE of 2,267C and an R2 of 0.935. SHAP analysis identifies vehicle age, year, power, and weight as the most influential predictors, with brand and model information providing additional refinement. The ranking changes for previously unseen brands. M3 performs below the brand-blind baseline, whereas few-shot calibration of M2 reduces MAE from 5,098C to 3,009C without retraining M1. evidence.title: Explainable and adaptive machine learning for used-car valuation: a modular framework for brand effects and pricing-risk analysis
evidence.abstract: Los precios de los vehículos usados reflejan no solo sus características técnicas y de uso, sino también la percepción de la marca, las condiciones del mercado y factores que no se observan directamente. Esto dificulta la estimación de un precio justo y genera un equilibrio entre precisión predictiva, interpretabilidad y capacidad de adaptación. Esta tesis analiza si separar el valor técnico del vehículo de los efectos de marca puede constituir una alternativa útil frente a los modelos que integran directamente la información de marca, especialmente cuando aparecen marcas no vistas previamente. Se comparan tres enfoques de valoración. Un modelo técnico ciego a la marca (M1) que estima el precio sin utilizar la marca ni del modelo. Un enfoque de ajuste modular (M2) que obtiene multiplicadores suavizados de marca-modelo a partir de los residuos de M1 y los aplica sin volver a entrenar el modelo técnico. Por otra parte, un modelo sensible a la marca (M3) que incorpora directamente la marca y el modelo mediante Categorical Boosting. M3 obtiene un rendimiento inferior al M1, mientras que la calibración de M2 reduce el MAE de 5.098C a 3.009C sin volver a entrenar M1. Además, los residuos se convierten en indicadores de riesgo de precios para priorizar desviaciones inusuales que requieran revisión humana. Por tanto, el marco debe interpretarse principalmente como un sistema de apoyo a la toma de decisiones para la valoración y revisión del inventario, y no como un mecanismo para determinar de forma definitiva si un vehículo está incorrectamente valorado. --ABSTRACT-- Used-car prices reflect not only technical and usage characteristics but also brand perception, market conditions, and factors that are not directly observed. The ranking changes for previously unseen brands. M3 performs below the brand-blind baseline, whereas few-shot calibration of M2 reduces MAE from 5,098C to 3,009C without retraining M1. These results suggest that direct brand integration is most effective when brands are represented during training, while modular calibration offers greater adaptability and transparency when they are not. Residuals are additionally converted into pricing-risk indicators for prioritising unusual deviations for human review. The framework is therefore best interpreted as a decision-support system for valuation and inventory review, rather than definitive evidence of mispricing.

title: Cognitive approach as a methodological basis for the application of neural network technologies in the training of specialists in adaptive physical culture
abstract: To understand how neural network tech-nologies can be integrated into the educational process, it is necessary to turn to the theoretical foundations of the cognitive approach, which offers a fundamentally differ-ent view of the nature of learning compared to the tra-ditional knowledge paradigm[1]. Unlike the knowledge paradigm, where the emphasis is on the translation and reproduction of information, the cognitive approach con-siders learning as a process of constructing students' own cognitive schemas. The neural network model per-forms a dual function: on the one hand, it acts as an infor-mation processing tool, on the other hand, it encourages students to reflect on their own thinking strategies. Thus, the cognitive approach creates a conceptual basis for the introduction of neural network technologies in the train-ing of specialists in adaptive physical culture, shifting the focus from knowledge transfer to the construction of cognitive schemes of professional activity. Objective of the study is to theoretically substanti-ate the cognitive approach as a methodological basis for the use of neural network technologies in the training of specialists in adaptive physical culture through the or-ganization of educational tasks in the full cognitive cycle ‘concrete – abstract – concrete.’ Results of the study and discussion. The cognitive approach, in our opinion, creates a methodological ba-sis for organizing the solution of educational tasks using neural network technologies. The peculiarity of this ap-proach is that the finished result generated by the neural network does not have its own theoretical foundations. The model gives a plausible answer, but does not explain from what theoretical premises it is derived. The educa-tional process based on cognitive logic naturally begins with the movement from the finished result to its founda-tions – that is, with analytical-regressive(abductive) rea-soning. In this first phase, the student reconstructs the patterns on which the result is based and gradually re-veals a concrete solution to an abstract theoretical basis. At the same time, the true assimilation of knowledge, according to the principle of ascending from the abstract to the concrete(V.V. Davydov, E.V. Ilyenkov), occurs through the movement of thought from the restored gen-eral foundation to its concrete manifestations. Therefore, the analytical phase should be followed by a second de-ductive phase, which assumes that the student returns from the found foundation to the concrete one in order to verify the initial result of the neural network and transfer the restored principle to new cases. Thus, the cognitive approach to working with neural network technologies is implemented as a complete cognitive cycle ‘concrete – abstract – concrete,’ in which inductive/abductive recon-struction and deductive verification act as complemen-tary phases. In the context of training specialists in adaptive physi-cal culture, this cycle is of particular importance. A neu-ral network can generate a rehabilitation program, select a set of exercises, and propose a method for correct-ing motor disorders. The first, analytical phase requires the future specialist to understand on what theoretical grounds the result is based, what patterns of develop-ment of people with disabilities are taken into account in it, what limitations and risks it carries. The second, de-ductive phase involves the use of already restored foun-dations to verify the correctness of the neural network's response and to justify decisions in new situations. It is the combination of these two phases that forms in the student not ‘knowledge about,’ but ‘knowledge of why’ as the ability not only to reproduce, but also to generate, as well as critically evaluate professional decisions. Сonclusions. The cognitive approach allows us to rethink the role of neural network technologies in the professional training of specialists in adaptive physi-cal culture. From the perspective of cognitive logic, the organization of solving educational tasks involves two complementary phases: analytical(reconstruction of the foundations of the generated result, the movement ‘from the concrete to the abstract’) and deductive(verification of the result and the transfer of the restored principle to new cases, the movement ‘from the abstract to the con-crete.’ Such a complete cycle allows rehabilitation pro-grams, sets of exercises and methods of correcting the physical condition of people with disabilities generated by the neural network to form the ability of a future spe-cialist to reconstruct their theoretical foundations, take into account the patterns of development of people with disabilities and deductively verify the correctness of the solution obtained.

title: MPGV Monitor: Dynamic Visualization of Seismic Data for Iceland
abstract: This thesis is presenting MPGV Monitor, it's a web application for exploring Icelandic earthquake activity from June 2020 onwards. It combines an interactive map with an Insights page so that users can inspect individual events and analyse selected records with the help of location, time, and magnitude. The published catalogue contains MPGV events from 1st of June 2020 with Magnitude -- Mw ≥ 3.0. Reconciliation combines the complementary strengths of two IMO sources: the improved moment-magnitude estimates in MPGV and the generally improved locations of reviewed records in the IMO Quakes API. MPGV determines catalogue membership. Where a unique match satisfies the temporal, spatial, and magnitude rules, the event retains the MPGV time and magnitude and uses Quakes API coordinates and depth. Events without an accepted match remain MPGV-only, and unmatched Quakes records do not independently enter the catalogue. Match status and field provenance are retained. The React frontend uses MapLibre GL and deck.gl for map display and earthquake interaction. Users can filter events, change visual encodings, inspect event details, and access eligible ShakeMap products. The connected Insights page provides summary statistics, charts, tables, and filtered export from the same catalogue. Depth analysis distinguishes matched Quakes API values from MPGV-only depths, which are labelled as unverified when included. This contribution is an implemented catalogue-exploration application that has a traceable data pipeline. Automated tests verify aspects of the software behaviour, but scientific matching accuracy, usability, accessibility, and performance at larger scales remain to be evaluated. MPGV Monitor is a research application and does not provide earthquake prediction or replace official operational monitoring.

title: Deep Learning for Early Prediction of Adverse Events in Intensive Care Units Using Electronic Health Records: A Methodological Review
abstract: Kai Wang,1,2 Hui Yan,1 Dongsheng Chen,3 Xin Tan,4 Han Chen,5 Xudong Lu,4 Huilong Duan,4 Shan Nan11Key Laboratory of Biomedical Engineering of Hainan Province, School of Biomedical Engineering, Hainan University, Haikou, People’s Republic of China; 2School of Information and Communication Engineering, Hainan University, Haikou, People’s Republic of China; 3Department of Clinical Laboratory, The 958th Hospital of Chinese People’s Liberation Army, Chongqing, People’s Republic of China; 4College of Biomedical Engineering and Instrumental Science, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, People’s Republic of China; 5Department of Information, Hainan Hospital of Chinese People’s Liberation Army General Hospital, Sanya, People’s Republic of ChinaCorrespondence: Shan Nan, Key Laboratory of Biomedical Engineering of Hainan Province, School of Biomedical Engineering, Hainan University, Haikou, People’s Republic of China, Email nanshan@zju.edu.cnPurpose: To provide a methodological synthesis of deep learning (DL) approaches for early prediction of preventable adverse events (AEs) in intensive care units (ICUs) using electronic health record (EHR) data, and to examine how intrinsic EHR data challenges affect model development, predictive performance, and clinical applicability.Methods: This review was designed as a methodological synthesis rather than a quantitative meta-analysis or statistical comparison. Seven databases were systematically searched to identify studies on early AE prediction in ICU settings using DL models. Eligible studies were screened based on predefined criteria, and data were extracted and synthesized qualitatively to analyze EHR data characteristics, DL architectures, and associated methodological challenges.Results: A total of 31 studies comprising 33 predictive models were included. These studies covered multiple preventable AEs, diverse ICU EHR datasets, and a range of DL architectures. Across studies with different prediction windows, reported AUROC values ranged from 0.75 to 0.95. Four studies used oversampling to address class imbalance. Despite the increasing use of advanced and hybrid architectures, three recurring methodological challenges remained: subtle early-stage risk signals, class imbalance, and heterogeneity. Overall, the effectiveness of DL-based AE prediction depends less on architectural novelty alone and more on whether models are explicitly designed around the data conditions under which preventable AEs emerge.Conclusion: Future studies should move beyond architecture-centered optimization and develop methodological strategies, such as multimodal learning, bias-aware modeling, and personalized prediction strategies. More attention should also be given to external and prospective validation, safe clinical use, and real-world effects on patient care and preventable harm.Keywords: deep learning, adverse events, intensive care unit, electronic health record data, early prediction

title: FileVault: A Multi-Tenant Storage and Persistent Memory Infrastructure for LLM Agents
abstract: LLM agents are stateless by default: les live in one system, vector memories in another, and neither survives between sessions without custom glue code. We present FileVault, a production storage system that unies le storage, semantic search, and persistent agent memory behind a single REST API and Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. FileVault indexes uploaded files automatically (fixed-window chunking, text-embedding-3-small embeddings) and stores both file chunks and key/value agent memories in PostgreSQL with pgvector HNSW indexes for approximate nearest-neighbor search. We evaluate FileVault's production retrieval path against three self-contained baselines exact (brute-force) cosine search, lexical (BM25) search, and no retrieval across three research questions: whether persistent memory survives across sessions as unrelated memories accumulate, whether semantic search outperforms lexical matching once queries are paraphrased away from a document's exact wording, and how retrieval latency and approximation quality scale as an agent's corpus grows toward FileVault's 50,000-chunk free-tier ceiling. We nd that memory recall stays at 100% up to 1,000 distractor memories and degrades to 93.3% at 5,000; that lexical search fails completely (0% recall) on paraphrased queries while semantic search stays at 100%, at roughly half the latency of exact search; and that HNSW's agreement with exact search on the true top-10 nearest neighbors declines from 100% to 6.4% as the corpus grows from 100 to 50,000 chunks, even as HNSW's own query latency stays two orders of magnitude below exact search's. We report this evaluation's methodology in full, including two confounds we caught and xed during the study, and conclude with concrete tuning recommendations for FileVault's HNSW conguration at scale. As a nal check before publication, we veried the live deployment directly and found it was, in fact, unreachable: fiveve independent, compounding bugs a database column-naming mismatch, an authentication middleware gate that blocked the entire agent API, two corrupted environment variables, and a recursive middleware request loop left core functionality broken in production despite a passing unit test suite throughout. We x all ve, add integration testing and a live smoke test to catch regressions of this kind going forward, and report the diagnostic process in full since none of it was visible to the retrieval-path evaluation above.

title: Cape Sengi: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Locomotion of Cape Sengi
abstract: This paper introduces Cape Sengi, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the unique locomotion strategy of the Cape Sengi ( *Xerostheria longicauda*), a small, insectivorous mammal native to southern Africa. The Cape Sengi's remarkable ability to efficiently navigate complex terrains by utilizing a hopping and sliding gait has been analyzed and translated into a novel algorithm designed for solving optimization problems. Cape Sengi employs a population-based search strategy, utilizing a 'hopping' mechanism to explore the solution space and a 'sliding' mechanism to refine solutions. The algorithm incorporates parameters mimicking the sengi's movement, such as hop length, hop frequency, and sliding distance, which are dynamically adjusted based on the fitness of the individuals in the population. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Cape Sengi through simulations on a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The core innovation lies in the synergistic combination of exploration and exploitation, leading to improved convergence rates and solution quality. Further research will explore the algorithm's adaptability to diverse problem structures and its potential for real-world applications.

title: ##基于多智能体协同的分布式资源调度
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to distributed resource scheduling leveraging the principles of multi-agent collaboration. The core claim is that by employing a multi-agent system, we can significantly improve resource utilization and overall system performance. The proposed mechanism involves constructing a system where individual agents are responsible for specific aspects of resource allocation. These agents then interact through both collaborative and competitive strategies, facilitating a dynamic and efficient distributed scheduling process. The novelty lies in the application of multi-agent coordination to this domain, offering a fundamentally new method compared to traditional centralized or simple distributed approaches. We explore the design considerations, potential challenges, and theoretical foundations underpinning this methodology, outlining a framework for future research and development in this area. The system described is designed to adapt to changing conditions and optimize resource allocation in a dynamic environment. ---

title: California Myotis: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Bat Echolocation
abstract: This paper presents California Myotis (CM), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the echolocation behavior of the California Myotis bat. CM leverages the bat's ability to navigate and forage in complex environments using sound emission and reception, translating these principles into a robust and efficient optimization process. The algorithm utilizes a dynamic parameter representation mirroring bat flight behavior, including position, velocity, and frequency modulation. CM incorporates a novel convergence mechanism based on the bat's avoidance of crowded areas, preventing premature convergence and promoting exploration. The algorithm's core components – the position update equation, the velocity update equation, and the convergence mechanism – are detailed. The performance of CM is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its competitive ability compared to established metaheuristic algorithms like Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA). The results highlight CM's adaptability and potential for application in diverse optimization challenges. Key words: Metaheuristic Optimization, Bat Echolocation, Optimization Algorithm, Evolutionary Algorithm, Convergence, Exploration.

The algorithm's core components – the position update equation, the velocity update equation, and the convergence mechanism – are detailed. The performance of CM is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its competitive ability compared to established metaheuristic algorithms like Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA). The results highlight CM's adaptability and potential for application in diverse optimization challenges. title: Brown-throated Sloth Metaheuristic Algorithm (BTS-MHA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Brown-throated Sloth Metaheuristic Algorithm (BTS-MHA), inspired by the unique movement patterns and foraging strategies of the brown-throated sloth (*Bradypus variegatus*). The algorithm leverages the sloth's deliberate, energy-efficient locomotion and its selective exploration of food resources to establish a robust optimization process. BTS-MHA incorporates a modified Levy flight mechanism for exploration, a dynamic inertia weight scheme informed by the sloth's varying levels of activity, and a novel constriction mechanism mimicking the sloth's cautious approach to new environments. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The results indicate that BTS-MHA exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm and the Particle Swarm Optimization, particularly in challenging, high-dimensional search spaces. Future research will focus on adaptive parameter tuning and incorporating biological insights to further enhance the algorithm's capabilities.

title: ## Broad-Cheeked Hopping Mouse Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Broad-Cheeked Hopping Mouse Algorithm" (BCHMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the broad-cheeked hopping mouse ( *Mus angleri*) – a rodent known for its efficient and adaptable movement across uneven terrain. The BCHMA leverages the mouse's characteristic hopping strategy, incorporating elements of exploration and exploitation within its search process. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach with adaptive parameter adjustments, mimicking the mouse's ability to adjust its hopping stride based on the terrain. Specifically, the algorithm employs a novel 'Stride Adjustment' mechanism, which dynamically modifies the step size of each individual based on the objective function value and the distance to the best solution. The performance of the BCHMA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive capabilities against established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results highlight the algorithm's potential for solving complex optimization problems with high dimensionality and non-convex landscapes. The core of the algorithm revolves around the concept of 'Terrain Mapping', where the search space is represented as a landscape and individuals 'hop' across this landscape, adapting their stride based on the perceived difficulty of the terrain. This paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and experimental results, providing a comprehensive analysis of its strengths and limitations.

title: Brazilian Arboreal Rice Rat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Arboreal Rice Rat Algorithm (ARRA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Brazilian arboreal rice rat (*Oenomys tropicalis*). This rodent's unique strategy of exploring the tree canopy in a seemingly random yet efficient manner provides a valuable blueprint for optimization. The ARRA leverages the rat's movement patterns, focusing on both exploration and exploitation phases, with modifications to incorporate dynamic step sizes and adaptive memory. The algorithm's core mechanism mimics the rat's ability to balance between moving to promising areas and revisiting previously explored regions. The performance of ARRA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, the Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. The results demonstrate that ARRA achieves competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Further analysis reveals the algorithm's sensitivity to key parameters, offering insights into its strengths and limitations. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential future research directions and the broader applicability of the ARRA concept to diverse optimization challenges.

title: Quantum Entanglement Encoding for Information Security
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon where two or more particles become linked and share the same fate, holds immense promise for revolutionizing information security. This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement to create robust information security protocols, specifically focusing on the encoding of data through entangled states. We investigate a novel approach combining quantum cryptography and topological data analysis to achieve a significant advancement in information safety. The core claim centers on the development of a secure data encoding system based on entangled quantum states, offering enhanced protection against data breaches and manipulation. This system leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to establish a fundamentally secure communication channel. The research examines the practical implications and challenges associated with implementing such a system, emphasizing its potential to counter the threats posed by increasingly powerful quantum computers.

title: Title: Non-Linear Quantum Field Theory with Adaptive Parameterization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel non-linear quantum field theory framework designed to enhance model accuracy and computational efficiency. Traditional field theories frequently rely on static, predefined parameters, limiting their applicability to specific physical scenarios. We propose a dynamic parameterization system that iteratively adjusts these parameters based on model performance, creating a feedback loop that continuously refines the model's fit. The core mechanism centers around a reinforcement learning-inspired feedback loop, evaluating the model's output against new data and optimizing parameter values to maximize predictive power. This approach overcomes the limitations of fixed parameter models, offering a more flexible and efficient framework for simulating complex quantum phenomena. The resulting model demonstrates improved performance across a range of benchmark problems, highlighting the potential for this adaptive approach in diverse physical contexts.

title: Blonde Capuchin: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of Blonde Capuchin Monkeys
abstract: This paper introduces Blonde Capuchin, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Blonde Capuchin monkeys. The algorithm leverages the monkey's strategy of exploring the environment, focusing on promising areas while simultaneously maintaining a degree of randomness to avoid premature convergence. Blonde Capuchin employs a combination of adaptive step-size control, a local search mechanism mimicking the monkey's selective attention, and a population-based approach reflecting the social dynamics observed in these primates. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a suite of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential advantages over existing metaheuristic methods. The core of Blonde Capuchin lies in the *attention coefficient*, which dynamically adjusts the exploration-exploitation balance, and the *proximity threshold*, governing the local search radius. We present a mathematical formulation of the algorithm and analyze its key parameters, providing a clear understanding of its operational principles. The primary objective is to achieve robust and efficient solutions across diverse optimization challenges. The proposed algorithm's ability to adapt to varying problem landscapes is a key feature, contributing to its overall performance. The results indicate that Blonde Capuchin provides a competitive alternative in tackling complex optimization problems.

title: VIENNA - Versatile Iterative Entity-alignment Combining Neural and Non-neural Approaches
abstract: Knowledge graphs (KGs) haben als Tools zur Speicherung und Ableitung neues Wissens rasant an Bedeutung gewonnen. Durch die zunehmende Popularität von Large Language Models (LLMs) wird deren Relevanz vermutlich weiter zunehmen, da sich beide Technologien komplementär ergänzen: Während LLMs implizites Wissen speichern und verarbeiten, bieten KGs explizite, strukturierte Informationen. Das zeigt sich in der aktuellen Forschung, etwa in Form von KG-enhanced LLMs und LLM-augmented KGs. Da KGs jedoch unvollständig sind, stellt sich die zentrale Herausforderung dar, verschiedene KGs aus unterschiedlichen Quellen zu vereinen. Diese als Entity Alignment bezeichnete Aufgabe ist aufgrund verschiedenster Schemata jedoch schwierig. Selbst wenn sich zwei verschiedene Quellen (KGs) auf dieselben Entitäten (Entities) der realen Welt beziehen, enthalten sie oft unterschiedliche Inhalte. In der aktuellen Forschung dominieren neuronale Methoden wie Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) und Knowledge Graph Embeddings, welche Entitäten in niederdimensionale Vektoren überführen, um sie anschließend auf Basis ihrer Vektorrepräsentationen zuvergleichen. Auch aufgrund des großen Erfolgs neuronaler Methoden bei anderen Aufgaben im Bereich von KGs wie Link Prediction (das Generieren neuer Relationen aufgrundvorhandener), vernachlässigt die aktuelle Literatur häufig nicht neuronale Methoden für Entity Alignment, die in der Forschung bis vor ein paar Jahren eine entscheidende Rolle spielten. Diese können je nach Anwendungsfall neuronale Ansätze sogar übertreffen, obwohl sie meist nur einen Bruchteil der Rechenressourcen beanspruchen. Die vorliegende Diplomarbeit zielt darauf ab, diese Lücke zu schließen, indem sie nicht-neuronale Methoden wieder aufgreift und diese mit modernen neuronalen Ansätzen kombiniert. Konkret wird ein modulares Framework namens VIENNA (Versatile Iterative Entity-alignment combining Neural and Non-neural Approaches) entwickelt. Dies nutzt sowohl neuronale Verfahren wie ClusterEA und BERT-INT als auch nicht-neuronale Techniken wie paris. Unser Framework, welches ohne Trainingsdaten auskommt, wird auf verschiedenen Datensätzen evaluiert, um Precision und Recall zu messen und zu prüfen, ob ein hybrider Ansatz reine neuronale Methoden übertreffen kann. Die Kombination dieser Verfahren verspricht eine umfassendere und flexiblere Lösung für Entity Alignmentund trägt damit zur Weiterentwicklung des Bereichs bei

title: Sarcoma Region of Interest (ROI) Images - Part 1
abstract: Bone and soft tissue (BST) tumors are a heterogeneous and rare group of mesenchymal neoplasms that pose significant diagnostic challenges owing to their complex morphologies and overlapping histological features. Despite rapid advances in digital pathology, most publicly available datasets predominantly focus on common epithelial tumors and offer a limited representation of BST tumors. To address this gap, we introduced the Pathologist-Annotated Image Retrieval dataset for Bone and Soft Tissue tumors (PAIR-BST), a dataset consisting of 2,252 pathologist-annotated regions of interest derived from 470 whole slide images obtained from 268 patients diagnosed with BST tumors. Each region was curated and annotated with multi-level labels, including 33 histologic diagnoses, 11 lines of differentiation, and 6 growth patterns, enabling comprehensive characterization of the morphological heterogeneity inherent to BST tumors. Benchmark experiments have demonstrated that pathology foundation models face challenges in identifying these tumors, particularly when distinguishing between tumor subtypes and growth patterns. PAIR-BST offers a high-quality, discriminative benchmark for the development and evaluation of pathology foundation models, specifically focusing on rare mesenchymal tumors.[Metadata Availability] Additional metadata containing specific coordinates for all ROIs (Regions of Interest) within the WSI, along with labels such as diagnosis for each, is available in a separate .csv file at: https://doi.org/10.25452/figshare.plus.33383509 (also linked in the related materials below). Find related datasets in the collection at https://doi.org/10.25452/figshare.plus.c.8223469

title: Personalized Federated Learning Algorithm Based on Multi-Layer Hypernetwork Aggregation
authors: LI Yang, JIANG Yi, CHEN Shuai, YAN Shichao, WANG Lei, MA Li
abstract: Personalized Federated Learning (pFL) algorithms have significant advantages in handling non-Independent and Identically Distributed (non-IID) datasets and enabling client-side model personalization. Hypernetwork-based pFL utilizes the client's own hypernetwork to achieve a personalized client model. However, the effect of sharing client-side hypernetwork parameters and client-side data on the accuracy of client-side personalized models remains unclear. A personalized Federated learning with Multi-layer Hypernetwork (pFedMHN) framework is proposed to optimize client models through the weighted aggregation of local and global hypernetworks. The server learns a global hypernetwork and each client's multi-layer local hypernetworks and then aggregates them. Clients use these aggregated hypernetwork parameters to iteratively update their models, resulting in more accurate personalized models. The experimental results show that on general public datasets, the pFedMHN outperforms the four benchmark algorithms in terms of accuracy, effectively solving the problems of data heterogeneity and model accuracy faced during personalized federated learning on non-IID datasets and achieving a more accurate personalized model for clients by utilizing hypernetwork parameters and client data sharing.

title: Temporal Expert-Based Reward Learning for Inverse Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Learning reward functions from expert demonstrations removes the need for manual reward engineering in reinforcement learning applied to robotic manipulation. Existing methods, however, require trajectory quality annotations, episode success labels, or produce implicit rewards that are difficult to inspect. This paper presents TEXB-IRL (Temporal EXpert-Based reward learning for Inverse Reinforcement Learning), which learns a dense neural reward function directly from unlabeled expert demonstrations. TEXB-IRL exploits intra-trajectory temporal ordering through two complementary objectives: a temporal consistency loss that enforces monotonically increasing reward along expert trajectories, and an expert-agent separation loss that anchors the reward scale. The policy is optimized with PPO over the learned reward. Preliminary experiments in simulation with the PAL TIAGo++ robot show competitive results against state of the art algorithms.

title: Chinese cyberbullying detection via multi-feature prompt learning
abstract: Most existing research on cyberbullying detection reduces the task to comment-level hate speech classification, overlooking its collective, event-driven, and dynamic nature. To address this limitation, we propose CDMPL, a multi-feature prompt learning framework for Chinese cyberbullying incident detection. CDMPL integrates textual features (semantic summaries generated by large language models) with temporal features (temporal behavioral patterns captured by a Dynamic Attention Truncation mechanism and an Autoformer-based time series encoder). These fused features are reformulated as a masked language modeling task, enhancing interpretability and robustness. We evaluate CDMPL on the only publicly available Chinese incident-level dataset, consisting of 86 cyberbullying and 109 non-cyberbullying events. Under a 15-shot setting, CDMPL achieves 84.79% accuracy and 84.05% F1-score, exceeding state-of-the-art large language models such as Doubao (71.91% F1) and ChatGPT-4o (70.06% F1) by more than 12%. Ablation studies further demonstrate the necessity of jointly modeling semantic and temporal features. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic study of Chinese incident-level cyberbullying detection, providing methodological and empirical advances for early detection and governance.
